God raised him from the dead: he walked out of the grave, conqueror of sin and death— Lord of Life! We are set right with God, given new life, and called to walk with him in freedom from sin's dominion. 26. Being both divine and human, Jesus is the only mediator. He alone paid the debt of our sin; there is no other Savior. We are chosen in Christ to become like him in every way. God’s electing love sustains our hope: God’s grace is free to save sinners who offer nothing but their need for mercy. 27. Jesus ascended in triumph, raising our humanity to the heavenly throne. All authority, glory, and sovereign power are given to him. There he hears our prayers and pleads our cause before the Father. Blessed are all who take refuge in him. The Spirit 28. At Pentecost, promises old and new are fulfilled. The ascended Jesus becomes the baptizer, drenching his followers with his Spirit, creating a new community where Father, Son, and Holy Spirit make their home. Revived and filled with the breath of God, women and men, young and old, dream dreams and see visions. 29. The Spirit renews our hearts and moves us to faith, leads us into truth, and helps us to pray, stands by us in our need, and makes our obedience fresh and vibrant. God the Spirit lavishes gifts on the church in astonishing variety— prophecy, encouragement, healing, teaching, service, tongues, discernment— equipping each member to build up the body of Christ and to serve our neighbors. 30. The Spirit gathers people from every tongue, tribe, and nation into the unity of the body of Christ. Anointed and sent by the Spirit, the church is thrust into the world, ambassadors of God’s peace, announcing forgiveness and reconciliation, proclaiming the good news of grace. Going before them and with them, the Spirit convinces the world of sin and pleads the cause of Christ. Men and women, impelled by the Spirit, go next door and far away into science and art, media and marketplace— every area of life, pointing to the reign of God with what they do and say. Revelation 31. God gives this world many ways to know him. The creation shows his power and majesty. He speaks through prophets, poets, and apostles, and, most eloquently, through the Son. The Spirit, active from the beginning, moved human beings to write the Word of God and opens our hearts to God’s voice. 32. The Bible is the Word of God, the record and tool of his redeeming work. It is the Word of truth, breath of God, fully reliable in leading us to know God and to walk with Jesus Christ in new life. 33. The Bible tells the story of God's mighty acts in the unfolding of covenant history. As one revelation in two testaments the Bible reveals God’s will and the sweep of God’s redeeming work. Illumined and equipped by the Spirit, disciples of Jesus hear and do the Word, witnessing to the good news that our world belongs to God, who loves it deeply. God's New People 34. In our world, where many journey alone, nameless in the bustling crowd, Satan and his evil forces seek whom they may scatter and isolate; but God, by his gracious choosing in Christ, gathers a new community— those who by God’s gift put their trust in Christ. In the new community all are welcome: the homeless come home, the broken find healing, the sinner makes a new start, the despised are esteemed, the least are honored, and the last are first. Here the Spirit guides and grace abounds. 35. The church is the fellowship of those who confess Jesus as Lord. She is the bride of Christ, his chosen partner, loved by Jesus and loving him: delighting in his presence, seeking him in prayer— silent before the mystery of his love. 36. Our new life in Christ is celebrated and nourished in the fellowship of congregations, where we praise God's name, hear the Word proclaimed, learn God’s ways, confess our sins, offer our prayers and gifts, and celebrate the sacraments. 37. God meets us in the sacraments, communicating grace to us by means of water, bread, and wine. In baptism, whether of the newly born or newly converted, God reminds and assures us of our union with Christ in covenant love, the washing away of our sin, and the gift of the Holy Spirit— expecting our love and trust in return. 38. In the Lord’s Supper, Christ offers his own crucified body and shed blood to his people, assuring them a share in his death and resurrection. By the Holy Spirit, he feeds us with his resurrection life and binds us to each other as we share one loaf and cup. We receive this food gladly, believing, as we eat, that Jesus is our life-giving food and drink and that he will come again to call us to the wedding feast of the Lamb. 39. The church is a gathering of forgiven sinners called to be holy. Saved by the patient grace of God, we deal patiently with others and together confess our need for grace and forgiveness. Restored in Christ’s presence, shaped by his life, this new community lives out the ongoing story of God’s reconciling love, announces the new creation, and works for a world of justice and peace. 40. We grieve that the church, which shares one Spirit, one faith, one hope, and spans all time, place, race, and language, has become a broken communion in a broken world. When we struggle for the truth of the gospel and for the righteousness God demands, we pray for wisdom and courage. When our pride or blindness hinders the unity of God's household, we seek forgiveness. We marvel that the Lord gathers the broken pieces to do his work and that he blesses us still with joy, new members, and surprising evidences of unity. We commit ourselves to seeking and expressing the oneness of all who follow Jesus, and we pray for brothers and sisters who suffer for the faith. The Mission of God's People 41. Joining the mission of God, the church is sent with the gospel of the kingdom to call everyone to know and follow Christ and to proclaim to all the assurance that in the name of Jesus there is forgiveness of sin and new life for all who repent and believe. The Spirit calls all members to embrace God’s mission in their neighborhoods and in the world: to feed the hungry, bring water to the thirsty, welcome the stranger, clothe the naked, care for the sick, and free the prisoner. We repent of leaving this work to a few, for this mission is central to our being. 42. In a world estranged from God, where happiness and peace are offered in many names and millions face confusing choices, we witness— with respect for followers of other ways— to the only one in whose name salvation is found: Jesus Christ. In Jesus, God reconciles the world to himself. God loves all creation; his compassion knows no bounds. 43. Jesus Christ rules over all. To follow this Lord is to serve him wherever we are without fitting in, light in darkness, salt in a spoiling world. 44. Life is a gift from God’s hand, who created all things. Receiving this gift thankfully, with reverence for the Creator, we protest and resist all that harms, abuses, or diminishes the gift of life, whether by abortion, pollution, gluttony, addiction, or foolish risks. Because it is a sacred trust, we treat all life with awe and respect, especially when it is most vulnerable— whether growing in the womb, touched by disability or disease, or drawing a last breath. When forced to make decisions at life’s raw edges, we seek wisdom in community, guided by God’s Word and Spirit. 45. Since God made us male and female in his image, we respect each other as equals, not flaunting or exploiting our sexuality. While our roles and capacities may differ, we are careful not to confine God’s gifts and calling to the shape of our cultural patterns or expectations. Sexuality is disordered in our fallen world— brokenness, abuse, pornography, and loneliness are the result— but Christ's renewing work gives hope for order and healing and surrounds suffering persons with compassionate community. 46. We are the family of God, serving Christ together in Christian community. Single for a time or a life, devoted to the work of God, we offer our love and service to the building of the kingdom. Married, in relationships of lifelong loyalty, we offer our lives to the same work: building the kingdom, teaching and modeling the ways of the Lord so our children may know Jesus as Lord and learn to use their gifts in lives of joyful service. In friendship and family life, singleness and marriage, as parents and children, we reflect the covenant love of God. We lament the prevalence of divorce and of selfish individualism in our societies. We belong to God. 47. Serving the Lord in whom all things hold together, we support sound education in our communities, and we foster schools and teaching in which God’s truth shines in all learning. All students, without regard to abilities, race, or wealth, bear God's image and deserve an education that helps them use their gifts fully. 48. Our work is a calling from God. We work for more than wages and manage for more than profit so that mutual respect and the just use of goods and skills may shape the workplace. While we earn or profit, we love our neighbors by providing useful products and services. In our global economy we advocate meaningful work and fair wages for all. Out of the Lord’s generosity to us, we give freely and gladly of our money and time. 49. Rest and leisure are gifts from God that relax us and set us free to discover and to explore. But we confess that often our addiction to busyness allows our tools and toys to invade our rest and that an internet world with its temptations distorts our leisure. Reminding each other that our Maker rested and gave us rest, we seek to rest more trustingly and to entertain ourselves more simply. 50. Grateful for advances in science and technology, we participate in their development, fostering care for creation and respect for the gift of life. We welcome discoveries that prevent or cure diseases and that help support healthy lives. We respect embryonic life, approaching each new discovery, whether of science or of medical technique, with careful thought, seeking the will of God. 51. We lament that our abuse of creation has brought lasting damage to the world we have been given: polluting streams and soil, poisoning the air, altering the climate, and damaging the earth. We commit ourselves to honor all God’s creatures and to protect them from abuse and extinction, for our world belongs to God. 52. We obey God first; we respect the authorities that rule, for they are established by God: we pray for our rulers, and we work to influence governments— resisting them only when Christ and conscience demand. We are thankful for the freedoms enjoyed by citizens of many lands; we grieve with those who live under oppression, and we seek for them the liberty to live without fear. 53. We call on all governments to do public justice and to protect the rights and freedoms of individuals, groups, and institutions so that each may do their tasks. We urge governments and pledge ourselves to safeguard children and the elderly from abuse and exploitation, to bring justice to the poor and oppressed, and to promote the freedom to speak, work, worship, and associate. 54. Followers of the Prince of Peace are called to be peacemakers, promoting harmony and order and restoring what is broken. We call on our governments to work for peace and to restore just relationships. We deplore the spread of weapons in our world and on our streets with the risks they bring and the horrors they threaten. We call on all nations to reduce their arsenals to what is needed in the defense of justice and freedom. We pledge to walk in ways of peace, confessing that our world belongs to God; he is our sure defense. New Creation 55. Our hope for a new creation is not tied to what humans can do, for we believe that one day every challenge to God’s rule will be crushed. His kingdom will fully come, and the Lord will rule. Come, Lord Jesus, come. 56. We long for that day when our bodies are raised, the Lord wipes away our tears, and we dwell forever in the presence of God. We will take our place in the new creation, where there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, and the Lord will be our light. Come, Lord Jesus, come. 57. On that day we will see our Savior face to face, sacrificed Lamb and triumphant King, just and gracious. He will set all things right, judge evil, and condemn the wicked. We face that day without fear, for the Judge is our Savior, whose shed blood declares us righteous. We live confidently, anticipating his coming, offering him our daily lives— our acts of kindness, our loyalty, and our love— knowing that he will weave even our sins and sorrows into his sovereign purpose. Come, Lord Jesus, come. 58. With the whole creation we join the song: “Worthy is the Lamb, who was slain, to receive power and wealth and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and praise!” He has made us a kingdom of priests to serve our God, and we will reign on earth. God will be all in all, righteousness and peace will flourish, everything will be made new, and every eye will see at last that our world belongs to God. Hallelujah! Come, Lord Jesus! For God’s ownership of all things, see Psalm 24:1 (quoted in 1 Cor. 10:26), Job 41:11, and Deuteronomy 10:14. That this is also “our world”—given to the human race to keep and care for—is one of the themes of the creation stories in Genesis 1 and 2. For God’s faithfulness, see, among many passages, Psalm 89, 117, 145; Romans 8:31-39; and Hebrews 10:23. For the victory of God in Christ and the rule of Christ, see 1 Corinthians 15:54-57, Philippians 2:9-11, and Revelation 1:13-18. For the Spirit’s work renewing creation, see Genesis 1 and Romans 8. Psalm 2 expresses the rebellious spirit of the human race. See also Romans 1-3. Ephesians 6:10-17 describes the struggle of believers with the spirits of the age. On testing the spirits, see 1 John 4. See Genesis 3; 9:8-16; Psalm 104, especially verse 30; Matthew 5:45; and Acts 14:17. For the promises of a Savior, see Genesis 3:15; Isaiah 7:14; 11:1-5; 42:1-7, 53; and Micah 5:2. For God’s fierce love, see Hosea 11, especially verses 10-11. For statements of the gospel message, see John 3:1-21, Acts 2:36-39, Romans 10:7-11, and Ephesians 2:1-10. For “firstfruits,” see Leviticus 23:9-14 and James 1:18. For references, see the first paragraph. See Genesis 1, where Creator, Word, and Spirit call creation into order. For the role of the Word in creation and Jesus as the Word, see John 1:1-14. On creation, besides Genesis 1 and 2, see Psalm 19; 33:6-9; and 104. For the image of God, see Genesis 1:26-27; 9:6; Ephesians 4:24; Colossians 3:10; and James 3:9. See Genesis 1:26-27, Galatians 3:26-28, and Acts 2:5-11. On how we treat the vulnerable among us as a measure of justice, see Isaiah 1:15-17 and James 1:27. For the providential care of God, see Isaiah 45:6-7, Matthew 6:25-34, and Luke 12:4-7. For the fall of humanity into sin, see Genesis 3. On the serpent, see, in addition to Genesis 3, Revelation 12:9 and 20:2. For the effects of the fall on humanity, see especially Romans 1:18-3:18. On the defacing of God’s image, see Romans 1:21-23; for the restoration of the image in Christ, see Romans 8:29, 2 Corinthians 3:18, Ephesians 4:22-24, and Colossians 3:10. Among many passages, see Psalm 14 and 53, Amos 1-2, Romans 1:28-32, and Galatians 5:19-21. See Psalm 62 and 89:28-37; Romans 5:3-11; 15:13; and Hebrews 11:1. For God’s response to sin, see Genesis 3:9-15, John 3:16, and Luke 1:68-75; for the aim to restore the kingdom, see Revelation 11:15. For God’s kindness to Adam and Eve, see Genesis 3:15-19. For God’s promise not to repeat the flood, see Genesis 9:8-17, 1 Peter 3, and 2 Peter 3; for the final renewal, see Revelation 21:1-5. For God’s promise to Abraham and to his people Israel, see Genesis 12:1-3, Deuteronomy 7-8, and Romans 9; for Abraham’s children as the light to the nations, see Micah 6:8 and Isaiah 60. For the scattering, see 2 Chronicles 36 and Isaiah 10:1-11; for the promises, see Isaiah 53, Jeremiah 31, and Ezekiel 36. For Jesus as the incarnate Son of God, see Luke 1:31-35, John 1:1-14, and Hebrews 1:2-3. In Romans 5:12-21, Christ is designated the second Adam. Hebrews 2:10-18 and 4:14-5:2 teach about his life of righteous humanity; the announcement of the kingdom is found, among other places, in Mark 1:1, 14, 15. For Jesus’ lifelong suffering, see Hebrews 5:7-10. All four of the gospel passion accounts portray the depths of his suffering on the cross. Jesus’ resurrection victory is proclaimed often, especially in Matthew 28:1-10 and 1 Corinthians 15:20-28. Christ is shown to be our mediator in 1 Timothy 2:5 and Hebrews 9:11-15, and our only Savior in John 14:6 and Acts 4:12. For our election in Christ to be like Christ, see Romans 8:29, 2 Corinthians 3:18, and Ephesians 1:3-4. For Christ’s universal authority and intercession as ascended Lord, see Matthew 28:18, Psalm 2:12, 1 John 2:1-2, and Hebrews 7:25. For the ascension of our humanity with him, see Hebrews 4:14-16; Ephesians 1:20-22; 2:6; and Colossians 3:1-4. On the fulfillment of promises at Pentecost along with dreams and visions, see Acts 2:16-21. On the ascended Jesus as baptizer and also the imagery of drenching in baptism of the Spirit, see Luke 3:16; John 1:32-33; 20:22; and Acts 2:32-33. On the Spirit creating a new community, note Acts 2:41-47 following Pentecost. On the Father, Son, and Spirit making their home with God’s people, see John 14:15-24. On the Spirit’s work of renewing our hearts, see Titus 3:4-7; moving us to faith, Romans 5:1-5; leading us into truth, John 16:13; helping us to pray, Romans 8:26-27; standing by us in our need, Hebrews 2:18; and making our obedience fresh and vibrant, Romans 8:1-11. On the Spirit’s gifts, see 1 Corinthians 12 and Romans 12:3-8. On the gathering of all nations, see Revelation 7:9-17; on the Spirit and the church’s mission, John 20:21-22, Luke 24:49, and Acts 1:8; on the church’s mission as ambassadors, 2 Corinthians 5:18-21; on the work of the Spirit in the world, John 16:7-11; and on the breadth of the church’s mission in the Spirit, Philippians 1:27-2:15. For general revelation, see Romans 1 and Acts 14; for the inspiration of the Bible, see 1 Timothy 3:14-17 and 2 Peter 1:16-21; and for the full revelation in Christ, see Hebrews 1 and Colossians 1. For the nature of Scripture, see Luke 1:1-4, John 20:30-31, Acts 8:26-39, James 1:18, and references in paragraph 31. For God’s mighty acts, see Acts 2 and 7; for our instruction, see Matthew 16:13-19, 1 Corinthians 10:1-11, 2 Timothy 3:14-17, and James 1:19-27. For the new community, see 1 Peter 2:4-7; for the attacks of Satan, 1 Peter 5:8-11; for the gracious welcome, Matthew 11:28-30 and 1 Peter 5:5-7. For the confession, see Matthew 10:32-33; for the church as the bride of Christ, see Ephesians 2:6; 5:21-33; 1 John 3:11-17; 4:13-21; and Revelation 21:9. For the church’s worship, see Matthew 6:5-15; 28:18-20; Acts 2:41-47; Romans 10; and 1 Corinthians 11:17-34. Matthew 3:13-17, with Matthew 28:19, establishes baptism as a gospel sacrament. That baptism is for children as well as adults and is accompanied by the gift of the Spirit is indicated in Acts 2:38-39. Titus 3:5 calls baptism a washing away of sins. Romans 6:1-11 and Galatians 3:27 show how it forms us as members of Christ. 1 Corinthians 10:1-10 indicates that baptism in itself is not a guarantee of salvation. Matthew 26:17-29 and parallels establish the Lord’s Supper as a gospel sacrament. On the meaning of the Lord’s Supper, see 1 Corinthians 5:7-8; 8:1-13; 10:14-21; and 11:23-26. See also Jesus’ strong words on his presence in the Lord’s Supper in John 6:48-58. On the church as a forgiven community called to be holy, see Ephesians 1:3-7; on dealing with one another patiently, Galatians 6:1-5 and Colossians 3:12-14; on the need for confession and restoration, 1 John 1:8-2:6; and on living out God’s reconciling love as part of a new creation, 2 Corinthians 5:17-21 and 1 John 3:16-17. On the unity of the church, see John 17:20-23 and Ephesians 2:11-22; 4:1-16. On our part in God’s mission, see Matthew 28:18-20, Luke 24:45-49, and John 17:18; on seeing our mission beyond our local community, Matthew 24:14 and Acts 13:1-3; on meeting the needs of people, Matthew 25:31-46 and Luke 4:18-19; and on the centrality of mission to our being, John 20:21. On the exclusive claims of Christ, see John 14:6 and Acts 4:12; on God’s love and compassion for the world, see Matthew 9:36-38 and John 3:16. On the rule of Christ over the whole world, see Philippians 2:9-11, Colossians 1:15-20, and Revelation 11:15; on being light, salt, and not fitting in, see Matthew 5:13-16 and Romans 12:1-2. On respect for all life, see Deuteronomy 5:17 and Psalm 104:14-30 and 139:14-16. Our very bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit: 1 Corinthians 6:19-20. Male and female, we are all made in God’s image: Genesis 1:26-27 and Galatians 3:27. On sexual disorder as a result of sin, see Romans 1:24 and 1 Corinthians 6:15-20. See the apostle Paul’s discussion of singleness and marriage in 1 Corinthians 7. On the importance of teaching and modeling the ways of the Lord, see Deuteronomy 6:4-9, Proverbs 22:6, and Ephesians 6:1-4. Jesus’ teaching on divorce is found in Matthew 19:1-12 and Mark 10:1-12. That we together reflect the love of God is taught in John 13:34-35 and all of 1 John. For the importance of education, see Deuteronomy 6:1-9 and Proverbs 4:1-9; for the need for God’s light, Psalm 119:105; for the central place of Christ, Colossians 1:17; for equal acceptance, James 2:1-13. For the place of work, see Genesis 2:15, Exodus 20:9, Ephesians 6:5-9, and 2 Thessalonians 3:6-13; for justice in the workplace, Ezekiel 34 and James 5:1-5; for generosity, 2 Corinthians 9 and 1 Thessalonians 4:9-12. For rest, see Genesis 2:2-3 and Deuteronomy 5:12-15; for the discriminating use of leisure, Philippians 4:8-9 and Ephesians 4:17-32. In Genesis 1:28-31 and 9:1-7, God gives to humanity the right and responsibility to develop and care for creation; for a reflection on the limitations of human technology and need for divine wisdom, see Job 28; for the continuing goodness of creation and the need for a prayerful approach to what we use of it, see 1 Timothy 4:4-5. Genesis 1:28-29; 7:1-5; Psalm 8; and Romans 8:18-25 teach that we are entrusted with caring for the earth. Romans 13:1-7 teaches respect for governing authorities (see also 1 Peter 2:13-17); Revelation 13 illustrates government gone wrong. Colossians 1:16 teaches that authority and power come from Christ; Ephesians 6:12 warns us that authority and power can become infected by evil. That governments are called to justice generally and that how a government treats the poor and the weak is a key indicator of a society’s commitment to justice is taught in all the prophets and in psalms like Psalm 72. Isaiah 2:1-4 expresses God’s will for peace, and Jesus said, “Blessed are the peacemakers . . .” (Matthew 5:9). On this hope, see 1 Peter 1:3-12, 2 Peter 3:3-13, 1 Thessalonians 4:13-5:11, and Revelation 11:15. For the coming of the kingdom of God, see Matthew 24, Acts 1:10-11, 1 Thessalonians 4:13-5:11, and Revelation 19:11-16. 1 Corinthians 15 speaks of the resurrection of the body, Revelation 21:4 of the wiping away of tears, and Revelation 21:22-27 of the light of heaven. Revelation 5 describes the Lion and the Lamb. For the just judgments of the Lord, see Revelation 19:1-10. A picture of the multitude of those declared righteous in Christ is found in Revelation 7:9-17. The concept of God weaving all things together is found, among other places, in Romans 8:28-39. For the imagery of this paragraph, see Exodus 19:5-6, Isaiah 40, 1 Peter 2:9-10, and Revelation 4-5.

documents.title: Form for the Baptism of the Children of Believers (I)
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/01 - Baptism/01 - Form for the Baptism of the Children of Believers (I).md
documents.text: Form for the Baptism of the Children of Believers (I) Brothers and sisters, as we come to the baptism of Full Name there are a few things worth thinking about regarding the sacrament of baptism. Why do we baptise? We baptise because baptism is a mark of discipleship and the sign of God's covenant of grace. After Jesus rose from the dead, but before He ascended to heaven, He commissioned His followers with this task: "Go and make disciples of all nations, baptising them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you". Throughout history God has marked His people with a special sign. God first made a covenant with Abraham, saying: "I will establish My covenant as an everlasting covenant between Me and you and your descendants after you for the generations to come, to be your God and the God of your descendants after you". The sign of that covenant was circumcision. When Jesus came, God made a new covenant with His people with a new sign to replace circumcision. The sign of this new covenant was baptism. In the same way as circumcision marked someone as being part of the covenant, so too baptism marks a person as being part of the renewed covenant in Jesus Christ. Baptism marks a person as a recipient of the covenant promise but also marks them as a disciple; someone who is learning to follow and obey Jesus. On the one hand, baptism is about the initiating, gracious promises of God, before anything we say or do. On the other hand, baptism is about an entry into the covenant community that follows the Lord of the covenant — Jesus Christ. As a result, a baptised child is not left to follow Jesus on their own. God calls a people, not just individuals, to be His treasured possession. This means a baptised child has the benefit of not only growing up in a Christian family that has the responsibility of discipling them, but also a church family that will spur them on in the faith. So, when we baptise someone in our church, we initiate them into the church and we make a commitment to disciple them; helping them to know and follow Jesus Christ. Why do we baptise with water? We baptise with water because it is a sign of washing and renewal. Just as water cleanses our bodies, so the blood of Christ cleanses us from our sins. Baptism is a physical sign, which is applied once, to point us to the spiritual cleansing of Jesus' sacrifice and the renewing work of the Holy Spirit — a work which is both complete and ongoing. Why do we baptise in the name of the Father, Son & Holy Spirit? We baptise in the name of the Father, Son & Holy Spirit because each person of the Trinity gives us certain promises in baptism. God the Father will adopt us as His children and heirs. God the Son will cover our sins with His perfect sacrifice. And God the Holy Spirit will dwell in us, helping us to obey, uniting us to the church, and sealing in us the promise of glory. By being baptised into the singular "name" of God, we state that God is unifying us as "one body", just as the Father, Son and Holy Spirit are One. This unity among us is shown outwardly by our shared baptism. Why do we baptise children of believers? We baptise the children of believers because they are, by God's grace, included in the covenant promise. As Peter says at Pentecost, after calling for repentance and baptism: "The promise is for you and your children and for all who are far off — for all whom the Lord our God will call." So, the children of believers, too, receive the sign of the covenant and discipleship because through their believing parents and the church community, they will learn about the great hope of this covenant: salvation through Jesus Christ. We baptise the children of believers because the Bible says they are considered "holy" through their believing parents (or parent). This means, they are set apart, along with God's holy church, "to declare the praises of Him who called us out of darkness and into His wonderful light." We don't baptise the children of believers because they have a personal faith — they may not be able to articulate whether they have that yet or not. Similarly, we don't baptise them because the parents' faith is somehow transferred to the child. And we don't baptise them because they are guaranteed to become Christians — rejection is a possibility, just as it is with baptised adults, and just as it was for those who were circumcised in Israel. No, we baptise children of believers because the sign of the new covenant belongs to them. So, we who follow Jesus must not hinder our children from coming to Him, but must disciple them; leading them, instructing them, and modelling to them that forgiveness and grace is found only in Jesus Christ. Baptism therefore places the child, the parents and the church under certain obligations. Name of child has a future obligation to accept, by faith, the washing away of their sins which Jesus has accomplished on the cross and to submit to Him as Lord. Name of Parents have an obligation to disciple the child as they grow to know the Lord Jesus. And the church has an obligation to partner with the parents to see this discipleship process through. Baptism is a gracious sign of God's initiating grace in salvation and an outward representation that this child has a place among us as his/her church. Now, having explained what baptism is and why this child should be baptised, we will ask the parents and the church to answer the following questions. Question to Parents: Names of Parents , as you have now heard, baptism is given to us by God because He made a covenant with us and our children. We baptise our children because it is a sacrament that Jesus Himself instituted for His covenant people. As parents, you are asked to answer the following questions: 1. Do you confess Jesus Christ as your Lord and Saviour, accept the promises of God, and affirm the truth of the Christian faith which is taught in the Bible and confessed in this church of Christ? 2. Do you believe that your child, though sinful by nature, is received by God in Christ as a member of His covenant and His church, and therefore ought to be baptised? 3. Do you promise, in reliance on the Holy Spirit and with the help of the Christian community, to do all in your power to instruct this child in the truth of the Christian faith and to lead him/her by your example to confess and follow Jesus Christ as their own Lord and Saviour? Answer: By the grace of God, we do. Question to the congregation (optionally have the congregation stand): Do you, fellow disciples of Jesus Christ, promise to receive Full Name in love? Will you pray for and help instruct him/her in the faith? Do you promise to model the Lord Jesus for him/her as a congregation, so that that he/she may grow up knowing and loving God, being surrounded by Christian examples? Answer: By the grace of God, we do. Baptism: In administering baptism, the minister shall say: Full Name , I baptise you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. (Prayer of thanksgiving can be offered here). Matthew 28:19-20 Genesis 17:7 Genesis 17:10 Matthew 28:20 Exodus 19:5-6 1 Peter 3:21 1 Corinthians 6:11 John 1:12-13 Hebrews 12:24 Ephesians 1:13-14 John 17:22-23 1 Corinthians 12:13 Acts 2:39 1 Corinthians 7:14 1 Peter 2:9 Genesis 17:7

documents.title: Form for the Baptism of the Children of Believers (II)
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/01 - Baptism/02 - Form for the Baptism of the Children of Believers (II).md
documents.text: Form for the Baptism of the Children of Believers (II) Note: With some modification, this Form could also be used for Adult Baptism. The minister shall say: Beloved brothers and sisters, Our risen Lord told His apostles, "...go and make disciples of all nations, baptising them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you." According to these words, there is a close connection between the proclamation of His kingdom and baptism. Those who accept the gospel with a believing heart receive in baptism the assurance that their sinful lives are cleansed by the Saviour's blood and are regenerated by the Holy Spirit. This is illustrated by the water used in baptism: for just as water cleanses our body, so the blood of Christ cleanses us from all sins. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit give promises and assurances in baptism. God the Father adopts us as His children and heirs. God the Son covers our sins with His perfect sacrifice. God the Holy Spirit dwells and works in us, recreating us into living members of Christ's body more and more until the great Day, when we shall at last be presented before God in the full beauty of Christ's spotless life. Baptism is administered only once, but remains valid throughout our life. Through the promises that our Lord makes to us in our baptism, He will enable us to grow in humility, so that He may become greater and we become less. In the covenant with the Lord it is not only He who makes promises, it is also we who have obligations. We are called to a new obedience. Our Lord both demands and encourages His covenant partners to serve Him, to seek His kingdom first, and to forsake the works of darkness. Even when we fall into sin through weakness, we should not despair, nor doubt His grace, but repent and return to our Father. Scripture calls Abraham the father of all believers. He was given the covenant sign of circumcision after he came to believe in God. However, God also commanded Abraham that this same sign of His grace be given to his small children. The grace of God is still the same today and includes our children in His covenant people. Scripture calls the children of believers holy and God's promises are for them as well as for us. God does not only call individuals but a people to be His very own. It is His will that all nations are to become His disciples. As brothers and sisters in Christ, we all — and Names of Parents in particular — must not hinder the children from coming to Jesus but must lead them to conversion and encourage them, instruct them and set them an example of Christian living. Prayer: Dear Father, be merciful to Full Name . May Your Holy Spirit unite him/her with Jesus Christ so that all the benefits of Christ's death and resurrection be his/hers. We rejoice with believing hearts as we see Your love again displayed in the baptism of this child. In the name of Jesus Christ our Saviour. Amen. The minister requests the parents to stand and says, addressing them by name: Name of Parents , since you have presented Name of Children for holy baptism, you are asked to answer the following questions before God and His people: 1. Do you confess Jesus Christ as your Lord and Saviour? Do you accept the promises of God, and affirm the truth of the Christian faith which is taught in the Bible and confessed in this church of Christ? 2. Do you believe that your child, though sinful by nature, is received by God in Christ as a member of His covenant and His church, and therefore ought to be baptised? 3. Do you promise, in reliance on the Holy Spirit and with the help of the Christian community, to do all in your power to instruct this child in the truth of the Christian faith and to lead him/her by your example to confess and follow Jesus Christ as his/her own Lord and Saviour? Answer: By the grace of God, we do. In administering baptism, the minister shall say: Full Name , I baptise you into the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. The minister invites the congregation to stand, and addresses them as follows: Do you, the people of the Lord, promise to receive Full Name in love, pray for him/her and help care for his/her instruction in the faith? Do you promise so to order your life and witness as a congregation that he/she may grow up in the knowledge and love of God, and be surrounded by Christian example and influence? Answer: By the grace of God, we do. A psalm or hymn is sung. The minister leads in the baptismal prayer: Lord our God, forever faithful to Your promise, we thank You for assuring us and our children again that You have forgiven us and received us as children in Christ. Grant wisdom and love to Name of Parents and to us all as we carry out the vows just made. We pray that You will guide our children throughout their lives and enable them to respond in faith to the gospel. Fill them with Your Spirit and make their lives fruitful. Uphold them in temptation, struggle and pain, and, when Jesus returns, let them celebrate with all the people of God Your greatness and goodness forever, in the joy of Your new creation. For Jesus' sake. Amen. Matthew 28:19 Romans 6:3-8; 1 John 2:2 John 1:12-13; Romans 8:17, 32; 1 John 3:1-3 Ephesians 5:26; Hebrews 13:12; 1 John 1:7; 2:2 1 Peter 1:2; 1 Thessalonians 5:22-23 John 3:30 Genesis 17:1; Romans 6:4 Matthew 6:33 Ephesians 5:8-20 Luke 15:18 Romans 4:11 Genesis 17:12 1 Corinthians 7:14 Acts 2:39 1 Peter 2:9 Matthew 28:19-20 Mark 10:14 Romans 6:3-4

documents.title: Form for the Baptism of Children of Believers (III)
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/01 - Baptism/03 - Form for the Baptism of Children of Believers (III).md
documents.text: Form for the Baptism of Children of Believers (III) — a baptismal service — CALL TO WORSHIP AND OPENING OF SERVICE M O give thanks to the LORD, call on His name, make known among the nations what He has done. C He remembers His covenant for ever, the word He commanded for a thousand generations. M Glory in His holy name, let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice. C Praise the LORD! Optional: silent prayer. M Our help is in the name of the LORD C Who made heaven and earth. M Grace to you and peace from God our Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ, in the fellowship of the Holy Spirit. C Amen. A psalm or hymn of praise is sung. M Our risen Lord Jesus said to His followers, "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me. Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptising them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And surely, I will be with you always, to the very end of the age." By giving us this sign of being washed with water our Lord tells us that we are unclean before God. Our sins need to be taken away if we are to enter the kingdom of God. Let us now come before the Lord in prayer and humbly confess our sins. C Almighty and most merciful Father, we have strayed from Your ways like lost sheep. We have left undone what we ought to have done, and we have done what we ought not to have done. We have followed our own ways and the desires of our own hearts. We have broken Your holy laws in our thoughts, words and deeds. Through our sins we deserve Your condemnation. O Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father, Who takes away the sin of the world, have mercy on us and hear our prayer. Amen. M People of God, in our baptism we are assured that the blood of Jesus Christ, God's Son, cleanses us of all sin, and that His Spirit renews us from day to day. We and our children are called back to the triune God in a restored covenant relationship. For when we are baptised into the name of the Father, God the Father assures us that He adopts us as His children and surrounds us with His love and care even in times of testing and trial. C God, our Father and Creator, we praise and thank You that You gave us life and adopted us as Your children. M When we are baptised into the name of the Son, God the Son assures us that through His death and resurrection we are set free from the condemnation of sin, and are made right with God by faith in Him alone. C Son of God, Saviour, we praise and thank You for Your sacrifice and victory. M When we are baptised into the name of the Holy Spirit, God the Holy Spirit assures us that He, the Giver of faith and new life, will live within us and change us by His power from day to day until at last we shall be presented spotless before God in the full splendour of life eternal. C Holy Spirit, our Guide and Companion, we praise and thank You for the life and hope You give us! M So God, who promises us all these things, calls us in this sacrament to begin living that new life in purity and holiness. He made a covenant with us: "I will be your God, you will be My people." He calls us to love Him with all our heart, soul, mind and strength. He calls us to be on His side in the battle against Satan and his works, both within ourselves and in the world around us. Jesus calls us to carry our cross in His footsteps and accept suffering as living members of His body. If then through weakness we fall into sin, it is He who calls us never to doubt His mercy nor to remain in sin or give ourselves up to despair. We are to remember joyfully that God's covenant with us is for ever, and so with His help we can overcome and are encouraged to go on in His service. C Sing BoW 474:3, or similar hymn or psalm: I heard the voice of Jesus say, 'I am this dark world's Light; look unto Me, your morn shall rise and all your days be bright!' I came to Jesus and I found in Him my Star, my Sun; and in that Light of life I'll walk till travelling days are done. M Scripture calls Abraham the father of all believers. He was given the covenant sign of circumcision after he came to believe in God. However, God also commanded Abraham that this same sign of His grace be given to his small children. The grace of God is still the same today and includes our children in His covenant people. Scripture calls the children of believers holy and God's promises are for them as well as for us. God does not only call individuals but a people to be His very own. It is His will that all nations are to become His disciples. Christian parents are entrusted with the vital task of bringing up their children in the Lord. They, with the help of God's people around them, are to lead them to faith and conversion by instruction in the holy ways of God, by prayer and the example of Christian living. Let us pray. We praise You, almighty Father, for saving the family of faith carried in the ark when the waters of the flood covered a rebellious world. We praise You, for setting Your people free as You led them safely through the waters of the Red Sea that swallowed up the oppressor. C Father, You are our God, we are Your people. M We praise You, Christ our Lord, for going down into the waters of Jordan and coming up to receive the Spirit; for sinking into the depth of our eternal death, to be raised up Lord of our life! C Christ Jesus, Son of God, You are our Shepherd, we are the sheep of Your pasture! M We praise You, Holy Spirit, for dwelling in us. We pray that You will separate us from sin and openly mark us with a faith that can stand the light of day and endure the dark of night. C Spirit of God, keep prompting us to glad obedience. M We ask You now for Name of Child that he/she may grow in grace and the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ, may learn what it means to walk joyfully in the footsteps of his/her Master, cheerfully enduring testing, trial and scorn of the godless, until at the end when God recreates the heaven and the earth he/she will see his/her Lord's face in never ending delight. C Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, You are our God, we are Your people. Amen. The minister requests the parents to stand and says, addressing them by name: Names of Parents , since you have presented Name of Child for holy baptism, you are asked to: (EITHER): answer the following questions before God and His people: 1. Do you confess Jesus Christ as your Lord and Saviour, accept the promises of God, and affirm the truth of the Christian faith which is taught in the Bible and confessed in this church of Christ? 2. Do you believe that your child, though sinful by nature, is received by God in Christ as a member of His covenant and His church, and therefore ought to be baptised? 3. Do you promise, in reliance on the Holy Spirit and with the help of the Christian community, to do all in your power to instruct this child in the truth of the Christian faith and to lead him/her by your example to confess and follow Jesus Christ as his/her own Lord and Saviour? Answer: By the grace of God, we do. (OR): make your baptismal vow before God and His people: (The parents say, if possible in unison) "We confess Jesus Christ as our Lord and Saviour, accept the promises of God, and affirm the truth of the Christian faith which is proclaimed in the Bible and confessed in the articles of our Christian faith as taught in this church of Jesus Christ. We believe that our child, Full Name though sinful by nature right from the beginning of his/her life, and consequently deserving of God's judgment and even eternal death is by God's mercy, holy in Christ and therefore, as a member of Christ's church, ought to be baptised. We realise that this child will have to confess Christ as his/her own Saviour. And so we promise, in reliance on the Holy Spirit and with the help of the Christian community, to do all in our power to instruct Full Name in the Christian faith, cause him/her to be so instructed, and to lead him/her by our example into a life of Christian discipleship." The minister says: Jesus said, "Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these." In administering baptism, the minister shall say: Full Name , I baptise you into the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. The minister invites the congregation to stand, and addresses them as follows: Do you, the people of the Lord, promise to receive Name of Child in love, pray for him/her and help care for his/her instruction in the faith? Do you promise so to order your life and witness as a congregation that he/she may grow up in the knowledge and love of God, and be surrounded by Christian example and influence? Answer: By the grace of God, we do. A psalm or hymn is sung. The minister leads in the baptismal prayer: Lord our God, forever faithful to Your promise, we thank You for again assuring us and our children that You have forgiven us and received us as children in Christ. Give wisdom and love to Names of Parents and to all of us as we carry out the vows just made. We pray that You will guide our children throughout their lives, and enable them to respond in faith to the gospel. Fill them with Your Spirit and make their lives fruitful. Uphold them in temptation, struggle and pain, and when Jesus returns, let them celebrate forever with all the people of God Your greatness and goodness, in the joy of Your new creation. For Jesus' sake. Amen. The service continues with the ministry of the Word. M = Minister, C = Congregation Psalm 105:1, 8, 3, 45 Matthew 28:18-20 Hebrews 8:10 Romans 4:11 Genesis 17:12 1 Corinthians 7:14 1 Peter 2:9 Matthew 28:19-20 1 Peter 3:20-21 1 Corinthians 10:1-2 Mark 10:14

documents.title: Form for the Baptism of the Children of Believers (IV)
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/01 - Baptism/04 - Form for the Baptism of the Children of Believers (IV).md
documents.text: Form for the Baptism of the Children of Believers (IV) The minister shall say: Congregation of our Lord Jesus Christ: What the Lord has revealed to us in His Word about holy baptism can be summarised in this way: First: Baptism teaches that we and our children are sinful from the time of conception and birth. This means that we are all under the judgment of God and for that reason cannot be members of His kingdom unless we are born again. Baptism teaches that sin has made us so impure that we must undergo a cleansing which only God can accomplish. Therefore, we ought to be displeased with ourselves, humble ourselves and turn to God for our salvation. Second: Baptism is a sign and seal that our sins are washed away through Jesus Christ. For this reason we are baptised into the name of God, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Our baptism into the name of God the Father is His assurance to us that He makes an everlasting covenant of grace with us and adopts us as His children and heirs. Therefore, He surrounds us with His goodness and protects us from evil or turns it to our benefit. When we are baptised into the name of the Son, we are assured by Christ Himself that He washes us in His blood from all our sins. Christ joins us to Himself so that we share in His death and resurrection. Through this union with Christ we are liberated from our sins and regarded as righteous before God. Baptism into the name of the Holy Spirit is the assurance that the Spirit of God makes His home within us. While living within us, the Spirit continually works to strengthen and deepen our union with Christ. He makes Christ's work of washing away our sins a reality in our lives. He also helps us each day to live the new life we have in Christ till we shall one Day be presented without the stain of sin among the assembly of the elect in life eternal. Third: Because all covenants have two sides, baptism also places us under obligation to live in obedience to God. We must cling to this one God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. We must trust Him and love Him with all our heart, soul, mind and strength. We must abandon our sinful way of life, put to death our old nature, and show by our lives that we belong to God. If we through weakness should fall into sin, we must not despair of God's grace, nor use our weakness as an excuse to keep on sinning. Baptism is a seal and totally reliable witness that God is always faithful to His covenant. Our children should not be denied the sacrament of baptism because of their inability to understand its meaning. Without their knowledge, our children not only share in Adam's condemnation, but are also received into God's favour in Christ. God's gracious attitude toward us and our children is revealed in what He said to Abraham, the father of all believers: "I will establish My covenant as an everlasting covenant between Me and you and your descendants after you for the generations to come, to be your God and the God of your descendants after you." The apostle Peter also confirms this with these words, "The promise is for you and your children and for all who are far off — for all whom the Lord our God will call." Therefore God formerly commanded that children be circumcised as a seal of the covenant and as a declaration that righteousness comes by faith. Christ also recognised that children are members of the covenant people when He took them in His arms, laid His hands on them, and blessed them. Since baptism has replaced circumcision, our children should be baptised as heirs of God's kingdom and of His covenant. It is the sacred duty of believing parents, aided by these great promises, to bring up their children instructing them in the fear of the Lord, by prayer and example of Christian living, and so by the Spirit of God lead them to conversion and faith. Let us turn to God, asking that in this baptism His name may be glorified, we may be comforted, and the church may be edified. Baptismal prayer: Almighty, eternal God, long ago You severely punished an unbelieving and unrepentant world by sending a flood. But You showed Your great mercy when You saved and protected believing Noah and his family. Baptism was again signified when You drowned the obstinate Pharaoh and his whole army in the Red Sea and brought Your people Israel through the sea on dry ground. We pray that in Your boundless mercy You will look upon these Your children with favour by bringing them, through Your Holy Spirit, into union with Your Son, Jesus Christ. May they be buried with Christ into His death and be raised with Him to new life. Give them true faith, firm hope and ardent love so that they may joyfully bear their cross as they daily follow Christ. Give these children the full assurance of Your grace so that when they leave this life and its constant struggle against the power of sin they may appear before the judgment seat of Christ without fear. We ask this in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one only God, lives and reigns forever. Amen. Address to Parents: Names of Parents , as you have now heard, baptism is given to us by God as proof that He does make a covenant with us and our children. We must, therefore, use the sacrament for the purpose that God intended and not out of custom, simply because it is expected of us, nor superstition thinking that the sign of baptism in itself guarantees salvation. You are asked to give an honest answer to these questions as a testimony that you are doing what God commands. First, do you acknowledge that our children, who are sinful from the time of conception and birth and therefore subject to the misery which sin brings, even the condemnation of God, are holy in Christ and so as members of His body ought to be baptised? Second, do you acknowledge that the teaching of the Old and New Testaments, summarised in the Apostles' Creed and our Confessions, and taught in this Christian church, is the true and complete doctrine of salvation? Third, do you sincerely promise to do all you can to teach these children, and to have them taught, this doctrine of salvation? Answer: By the grace of God, we do. In administering baptism, the minister shall say: Full Name , I baptise you into the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. The minister invites the congregation to stand, and addresses them as follows: Do you, the people of the Lord, promise to receive Full Name in love, pray for him/her and help care for his/her instruction in the faith? Do you promise so to order your life and witness as a congregation that he/she may grow up in the knowledge and love of God, and be surrounded by Christian example and influence? Answer: By the grace of God, we do. A psalm or hymn is sung. Prayer of thanksgiving: Almighty God and merciful Father, we thank You and praise Your name for having forgiven our sins through the blood of Your dear Son, Jesus Christ. We thank You for uniting us with Christ through Your Holy Spirit and adopting us as Your children, and we thank You for sealing and confirming these blessings to us and our children in the sacrament of baptism. We pray, O Lord, that You will always govern these children by Your Holy Spirit. May they, through Your guidance, be so nurtured in the Christian faith and godliness as to grow and develop in Jesus Christ. Help them see Your fatherly goodness and mercy which surrounds us all. Make them champions of righteousness under the direction of Jesus Christ, our only Teacher, King and High Priest. Give them the courage to fight against and overcome sin, the devil and his whole dominion. May their lives become an eternal song of praise to You, the one only true God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Amen. Genesis 17:7 Acts 2:39 Romans 4:11 Mark 10:16 Ephesians 6:1-4 Psalm 111:10; Proverbs 1:7; Joshua 24:15 2 Samuel 12:16; 1 Chronicles 29:19; Job 1:5; Matthew 17:15; Mark 7:26 1 Kings 9:4; 2 Timothy 1:5 2 Timothy 1:5; Matthew 4:17; Luke 24:47; Titus 2:11-14; 2 Peter 1:10 1 Peter 3:20-21; 1 Corinthians 10:1-2 1 Corinthians 7:14

documents.title: Form for the Baptism of Adults
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/01 - Baptism/05 - Form for the Baptism of Adults.md
documents.text: Form for the Baptism of Adults — a baptismal service — ____________________________________________________ NOTE: Sessions can combine a Form for the Baptism of the Children of Believers with the Form for Public Profession of Faith. If it is an adult baptism that does not include children, the segment of the Form for Baptism dealing with children being in the covenant can be omitted. In this Form: (p) before a paragraph means: This is to be said where public profession of faith is also made by baptised members. (c) before a paragraph means: This is to be said where both adults and their children receive baptism. It is meaningful and Scriptural, when there are such children, that they receive the sacrament in the same service as their parents. ____________________________________________________ CALL TO WORSHIP AND OPENING OF SERVICE M Shout for joy to the LORD, all the earth, serve the Lord with gladness; come before Him with joyful songs. Know that the LORD is God! C It is He who made us, and we are His; we are His people, the sheep of His pasture. M Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise; give thanks to Him and praise His name. C For the LORD is good and His love endures forever; His faithfulness continues through all generations. M With joy, you will draw water from the wells of salvation! Optional: silent prayer. M Our help is in the name of the Lord C Who made heaven and earth. M Who faithfully keeps His word C and never forsakes the works of His hands. M Grace to you and peace from God our Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ, in the fellowship of the Holy Spirit. C Amen. A psalm or hymn of praise is sung. M Our risen Lord Jesus said to His followers: "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me. Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptising them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And surely, I will be with you always, to the very end of the age." By giving us this sign of being washed with water our Lord tells us that we are unclean before God. Our sins need to be taken away if we are to enter the kingdom of God. Let us come before the Lord in prayer and humbly confess our sins. C Almighty and most merciful Father, we have strayed from Your ways like lost sheep. We have left undone what we ought to have done, and we have done what we ought not to have done. We have followed our own ways and the desires of our own hearts. We have broken Your holy laws in our thoughts, words and deeds. Through our sins we have deserved Your condemnation. O Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father, Who takes away the sin of the world, have mercy on us and hear our prayer. Amen. M People of God, in our baptism we are assured that the blood of Jesus Christ, God's Son, cleanses us of all sin, and that His Spirit renews us from day to day. We and our children are called back to the triune God in a restored covenant relationship. For when we are baptised into the name of the Father, God the Father assures us that He adopts us as His children and surrounds us with His love and care even in times of testing and trial. C God, our Father and Creator, we praise and thank You that You gave us life and adopted us as Your children. M When we are baptised into the name of the Son, God the Son assures us that through His death and resurrection we are set free from the condemnation of sin, and are made right with God by faith in Him alone. C Son of God, Saviour, we praise and thank You for Your sacrifice and victory! M When we are baptised into the name of the Holy Spirit, God the Holy Spirit assures us that He, the Giver of faith and new life, will live within us and change us by His power from day to day until at last we shall be presented spotless before God in the full splendour of life eternal. C Holy Spirit, our Guide and Companion, we praise and thank You for the life and hope You give us! M So God, who promises us all these things, calls us in this sacrament to begin living that new life in purity and holiness. He made a covenant with us: "I will be your God, you will be My people." He calls us to love Him with all our heart, soul, mind and strength. He calls us to be on His side in the battle against Satan and his works, both within ourselves and in the world around us. Jesus calls us to carry our cross in His footsteps and accept suffering as living members of His body. If then through weakness we fall into sin, it is He who calls us never to doubt His mercy nor to remain in sin or give ourselves up to despair. We are to remember joyfully that God's covenant with us is for ever, and so with His help we can overcome and are encouraged to go on in His service. C Sing Psalm 79a:2 or similar psalm or hymn. O LORD, by grace we are Your chosen nation; we are Your sheep, Your new-born generation, You are our Shepherd, and will ever lead us and in the bounty of Your pastures feed us. Then father tells to son the deeds that You have done: Your great redemption's story! So sounds Your praise along in one unbroken song to Your unending glory! THE SERVICE OF THE WORD After the sermon a psalm or hymn is sung. Then an elder shall say: Brothers and sisters in Christ, It gives me great joy, on behalf of Session, to present to you Name(s) of Candidate(s) for Adult Baptism , who has expressed the desire to join this Christian church and has been instructed in the teachings of our faith. He has professed his faith before Session and now wants to do so publicly before this congregation and so receive the sacrament of baptism (c) with his children Name(s) of Child(ren) . (p) We also gladly present to you the following baptised members who, having been nurtured in the Christian faith, now seeks full communicant membership in this church: Name(s) of Baptised Member(s) . He, too, has professed his faith before Session and desires to do so before you all. We thank our Lord who in His grace has called him and brought him to this turning point in his life, trusting that He who began a good work in him will carry it on to completion until the Day of Christ Jesus. PROFESSION It is suggested that, as the minister calls each individual candidate by name, (s)he arises and faces the congregation. Name of Candidate , the Lord Jesus says: "You did not choose Me, but I chose you to go and bear fruit — fruit that will last." "Whoever acknowledges Me before men, I will also acknowledge him before My Father in heaven." It is God in His sovereign love who chose you, (p) who keeps His covenant of grace with you, who gives faith and unites you with Jesus Christ, and calls you into the full fellowship of His church. In the presence of God and His people, we now invite you to profess your faith in Him. At this point one of two procedures can be followed: EITHER: each candidate says the following. Candidates may be encouraged to use their own words but the following areas are to be covered substantially: OR: alternatively, if there are too many people for each to speak or it is deemed inappropriate for each to make a full verbal confession, the minister may address the following questions: 1. I profess that Jesus Christ is my Lord and Saviour, and I want to follow and serve Him as His disciple. I believe He is the Son of God sent to redeem the world. I love and trust Him as the One who saves me from sin; I continue to turn from my rebellion against my Lord, and embrace Him as Lord of my life with repentance and joy. 1. Do you believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God sent to redeem the world; do you love and trust Him as the One who saves you from your sin; will you continue to turn from your rebellion against your Lord, and do you with repentance and joy embrace Him as the Lord of your life? 2. I acknowledge that the teaching of the Old and New Testaments, summarised in the Apostles' Creed and our Confessions and taught in this Christian church, is the true and complete doctrine of salvation. 2. Do you acknowledge that the teaching of the Old and New Testaments, summarised in the Apostles' Creed and our Confessions and taught in this Christian church, is the true and complete doctrine of salvation? (p) 3. I accept the gracious promises of God sealed to me in my baptism and affirm my union with Christ and His church which baptism signifies. (p) 3. And, baptised members, do you accept the gracious promises of God sealed to you in your baptism and do you affirm your union with Christ and His church which baptism signifies? 4. I promise to do all I can, with the help of the Holy Spirit, to strengthen my love and commitment to Christ by sharing faithfully in the life of the church and its means of grace, honouring and submitting to its supervision and discipline, and I join with the people of God in doing the work of the Lord wherever I am. 4. Do you promise to do all you can, with the help of the Holy Spirit, to strengthen your love and commitment to Christ by sharing faithfully in the life of the church and its means of grace, honouring and submitting to its supervision and discipline, and do you join with the people of God in doing the work of the Lord wherever you are? Name(s) of Candidate(s) , what is your answer to these questions? Each replies in turn: I profess that Jesus Christ is my Lord and Saviour and I want to follow and serve Him as His disciple. So, with all my heart, by the grace of God, I say "Yes!" to these questions. The minister addresses each person individually after his/her profession is made by way of: — an individual text, — a word of promise, exhortation or doxology, — and, if appropriate, an individual personal word. At this point a psalm or hymn may be sung. Then all are requested to be seated. M (c) God graciously includes our children in His covenant, and all His promises are for them as well as for us. Jesus Himself took little children in His arms and blessed them, and the apostle Paul said that children of believers are holy. So, just as the children of the Old Covenant received the sign of circumcision, our children are given, with us, the sign of baptism: "you and your house-hold!" We are, therefore, always to teach our young ones that they have been set apart by baptism as God's own children. In all cases, the minister continues: Let us pray. We praise You, Almighty Father, for saving the family of faith carried in the ark when the waters of the flood covered a rebellious world. We praise You, for setting Your people free as You led them safely through the waters of the Red Sea that swallowed up the oppressor. C Father, You are our God, we are Your people. M We praise You, Christ our Lord, for going down into the waters of Jordan and coming up to receive the Spirit; for sinking into the depth of our eternal death, to be raised up Lord of our life! C Christ Jesus, Son of God, You are our Shepherd, we are the sheep of Your pasture! M We praise You, Holy Spirit, for dwelling in us. We pray that You will separate us from sin and openly mark us with a faith that can stand the light of day and endure the dark of night. C Spirit of God, keep prompting us to glad obedience. M We pray now for Names of all to be baptised, including children (if any) , that he, daily dying to sin and raised to the new life You give, may carry his cross joyfully in the Master's footsteps, till on the great Day of Jesus he, too, will see His face in never-ending delight. C Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, You are our God, we are Your people. Amen. Minister, addressing adult(s) to be baptised: Do you now wish to be baptised in the name of the triune God, and will you receive your baptism as a sign and seal that God accepts you in Christ, forgives all your sins, and incorporates you into His church? Each confessor: I do, with all my heart. The Minister continues: (c) Do you furthermore believe that your child(ren) Name(s) of Child(ren) , though sinful by nature right from the beginning of his life and consequently deserving of God's judgment and even eternal death is, by God's mercy, holy in Christ and therefore, as a member of Christ's church, ought to be baptised? Finally, do you promise, in reliance on the Holy Spirit and with the help of the Christian community, to do all in your power to instruct Name(s) of Child(ren) in the Christian faith, cause him to be so instructed, and to lead him by your example into a life of Christian discipleship? Parents: By the grace of God, we do. When both adults and child(ren) are to be baptised, the adults receive the sacrament first. They shall kneel and receive the baptism on their foreheads. They then shall arise and present their child(ren) for baptism. M Full Name , I baptise you into the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Congregation, please arise. Do you, the people of the Lord, promise to receive Names of those baptised, both young and old in love into your fellowship as members of the body of Christ, and do you promise to encourage them in doing the work of the Lord? C By the grace of God, we do. M I now ask all those baptised members who have just professed their faith to join those who have just been baptised. Raising his hands over the confessor(s) or laying his hand(s) upon his/her head: The God of all grace, who has called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore you and make you strong, firm and steadfast. To Him be the power for ever and ever! THE LORD BLESS YOU AND KEEP YOU. THE LORD MAKE HIS FACE TO SHINE UPON YOU AND BE GRACIOUS TO YOU; THE LORD TURN HIS FACE TOWARD YOU AND GIVE YOU PEACE. Amen. An elder then addresses the confessor(s): In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ I now welcome you all to full communicant participation in the life of the church. I welcome you to its responsibilities, its privileges, its sufferings and its joys. C Thanks be to God! We rejoice in your profession and promise you our love, encouragement and prayers. A psalm or hymn is sung. Then there could be a time of symbolising the welcome, e.g., wishing each other God's peace, shaking hands, giving of gifts or allocation of tasks. It would be very meaningful if, in the same service or in another service on the same day, the Lord's Supper is celebrated. M Let us give thanks to the Lord. Our Father in heaven, we thank You for Jesus Christ, for the new life given in Him, and for the one faith, one hope, and one baptism which your people have shared through the ages. We rejoice that Name of Adults Baptised is now one with Your church and that we have received him as a members of this congregation. (p) We praise You that Baptised members who have professed their faith have come to see the riches You promised them when they were children, and have responded in faith and joy to the call of their Saviour and Lord. (c) Enable Names of Children who have just received the sacrament of baptism to stand up, in Your good time, among Your people and openly acknowledge Your great goodness and grace in Jesus Christ. To that end, Lord, give wisdom to their parents and all of us to guide them in Your ways. Encourage us all to fight the works of Satan and give us endurance in trial and hardship. Then, when the great Day of Jesus comes, we will meet Him with joy and celebrate with all Your people the feast of Your eternal presence and glory. Through Jesus Christ our Lord, Who taught us to pray: C Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name, Your Kingdom come, Your will be done on earth as in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. Forgive us our sins, as we forgive those who sin against us. Lead us not into temptation but deliver us from the evil one. For the kingdom, the power and the glory are Yours, now and for ever. Amen. M = Minister C = Congregation, in unison Psalm 100; Isaiah 12:3 Matthew 28:18-20 Hebrews 8:10 Philippians 1:6 John 15:16 Matthew 10:32 1 Corinthians 7:14 Acts 2:39; 16:31-33; 1 Corinthians 1:16; see also Romans 4:11-12 and Genesis 17:12; Mark 10:13-16; 1 Corinthians 7:14 1 Peter 3:20-21 1 Corinthians 10:1-2 Romans 3:23; 6:23 1 Corinthians 7:14 1 Peter 5:10-11; Numbers 6:24-26
