documents.text: Form for the Public Profession of Faith PRESENTATION An elder representing Session introduces the candidates: Congregation of our Lord Jesus Christ, Today we are privileged to present to you the following baptised people who wish to profess their faith in Jesus Christ as Lord and Saviour and to become communicant members, sharing in all the rights and responsibilities that belong to full and active membership in the church of Christ: Name(s) of Candidate(s) . When they were baptised, God made clear His claim on them as His own and they were received into the church. Through God's Word and Spirit they have come to faith in Christ and an understanding of their place in God's covenant of grace. Now they wish to share fully in the life of this congregation and of the whole world-wide Church of God. So today they will publicly accept and confirm what was sealed in their baptism, profess their faith in the Lord Jesus and offer themselves to God as His willing servants. We thank God for giving them this desire and pray that as we now witness their profession, He will favour us with the presence and guidance of His Holy Spirit. PROFESSION It is suggested that, as the minister or elder calls each individual candidate by name, he/she arises and faces the congregation. The Minister continues: Name of each Candidate , the Lord Jesus says: "You did not choose Me, but I chose you to go and bear fruit — fruit that will last." "Whoever acknowledges Me before men, I will also acknowledge him before My Father in heaven." It is God's sovereign grace and love that made you enter life as children of His people, receiving baptism as a sign of His covenant when you were still very young. It is God's sovereign grace and love that made you hear the good news of Christ Jesus in years gone by, and so you were not left ignorant of the open Way to the Father. It is God's sovereign grace and love that led you to repentance, to make you humbly see your need of the gospel of salvation. It is God's sovereign grace and love that calls us all, who were doomed to die eternally, to live instead and be bearers of hope and life in a dark world. In the presence of God and His people, we now invite you to profess your faith in Him. At this point one of two procedures can be followed: EITHER: OR: Each candidate says the following. Candidates may be encouraged to use their own words but the following areas are to be covered substantially Alternatively, if there are too many people for each to speak or it is deemed inappropriate for each to make his/her confession, the minister or elder may address the following questions: 1. I profess that Jesus Christ is my Lord and Saviour, and I want to follow and serve Him as His disciple. I believe He is the Son of God sent to redeem the world. I love and trust Him as the One who saves me from sin; I continue to turn from my rebellion against my Lord, and embrace Him as Lord of my life with repentance and joy. 1. Do you believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God sent to redeem the world; do you love and trust Him as the One who saves you from your sin; will you continue to turn from your rebellion against your Lord, and do you with repentance and joy embrace Him as the Lord of your life? 2. I acknowledge that the teaching of the Old and New Testaments, summarised in the Apostles' Creed and our Confessions, and taught in this Christian church, is the true and complete doctrine of salvation. 2. Do you acknowledge that the teaching of the Old and New Testaments, summarised in the Apostles' Creed and our Confessions, and taught in this Christian church, is the true and complete doctrine of salvation? 3. I accept the gracious promises of God sealed to me in my baptism and affirm my union with Christ and His church which baptism signifies. 3. Do you accept the gracious promises of God sealed to you in your baptism and do you affirm your union with Christ and His church which baptism signifies? 4. I promise to do all I can, with the help of the Holy Spirit, to strengthen my love and commitment to Christ by sharing faithfully in the life of the church and its means of grace, honouring and submitting to its supervision and discipline, and I join with the people of God in doing the work of the Lord wherever I am. 4. Do you promise to do all you can, with the help of the Holy Spirit, to strengthen your love and commitment to Christ by sharing faithfully in the life of the church and its means of grace, honouring and submitting to its supervision and discipline, and do you join with the people of God in doing the work of the Lord wherever you are? Name of each Candidate , what is your answer to these questions? Each candidate replies in turn: I profess that Jesus Christ is my Lord and Saviour and I want to follow and serve Him as His disciple. So, with all my heart, by the grace of God, I say "Yes!" to these questions. The minister or elder addresses each person individually after profession is made by way of: — an individual text, — a word of promise, exhortation or doxology, — and, if appropriate, an individual personal word. And/or after all have made their profession: Be strong in the Lord and in His mighty power. Let the Word of Christ dwell in you richly. Whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him. And the God of all grace, who called you to His eternal glory in Christ, after you have suffered a little while, will Himself restore you and make you strong, firm and steadfast. To Him be the power for ever and ever. Amen. PRAYER AND BLESSING Optional: candidates kneel; elders and parents may be invited to gather round them. The minister leads in prayer and blessing: Lord, our God, we thank You for Your Word and Spirit through which we know Jesus Christ as Lord and Saviour. May those who professed Your name today never cease to wonder at all that You have done for them. Help them to continue firmly in the faith, to bear witness to Your love, and let the Holy Spirit shape their lives. Take them, Good Shepherd, into Your care so that they may loyally endure opposition in serving You. May we, with all Your children, live together in the joy and power of Your Holy Spirit. We ask this, in the name of the Lord Jesus and in the hope of His coming. THE LORD BLESS YOU AND KEEP YOU. THE LORD MAKE HIS FACE TO SHINE UPON YOU AND BE GRACIOUS TO YOU; THE LORD TURN HIS FACE TOWARD YOU AND GIVE YOU PEACE. Amen. CONGREGATIONAL WELCOME Candidates and congregation are invited to stand. The elder representing Session shall say: In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ we now welcome you to full participation in the life of the church, the privileges of communion, the responsibility of exercising your gifts, the fellowship of its joys and sufferings. The whole congregation responds: Thanks be to God! We rejoice in your profession and promise you our love, encouragement and prayers. The minister invites the congregation to affirm together what we believe in the Apostles' Creed. A psalm or hymn is sung. There could then be a time of symbolising the welcome, e.g., wishing each other God's peace, shaking hands, giving of gifts or allocation of tasks. It would be very meaningful if, in the same service or in another service on the same day, the Lord's Supper is celebrated. John 15:16 Matthew 10:32 Ephesians 6:10; Colossians 3:16-17; 1 Peter 5:10-11 Numbers 6:24-26

documents.title: Form for the Preparation of the Lord's Supper (I)
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/03 - The Lord's Supper/01 - Form for the Preparation of the Lord's Supper (I).md
documents.text: Form For The Preparation Of The Lord's Supper (I) The minister or elder leading the service says: As we prepare to celebrate the Lord's Supper, let us remember that Scripture calls us to examine ourselves before God. Although there is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus, it is possible to eat and drink a judgment on ourselves if we approach His holy table without realising properly what we are to do there. Scripture says that, in this sacrament, "we proclaim the death of the Lord until He comes." In sorrow and repentance we are to see how our sins caused Jesus' death, in thankfulness how He fully saves us by His death, in joyful service how we are to respond to our Saviour's death, and in love how we can help others to find peace in that death. The responses between [ ] may be omitted, or said by the leader of the service, or said by all. In the latter case the leader of the service says: [Let us now say together: Show us Your ways, O LORD, teach us Your paths; guide us in Your truth and teach us, for You are God our Saviour, and our hope is in You, all day long.] Who are we to proclaim the death of Christ? We, whose sins are the cause of it! For our transgressions He was pierced, and for our iniquities He was crushed. Only in utter humility can we properly celebrate the Supper of our Lord, knowing that "God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble." [Out of the depths we cry to You, O LORD, O LORD, hear our voice. Let Your ears be attentive to our cry for mercy. If You, O LORD, kept a record of sins, O LORD, who could stand? ] The marvellous news of the gospel comes to those who humble themselves before God: When we were still helpless, Christ died for the ungodly. This is how God showed His love among us, He sent His one and only Son into the world that we might live through Him. This is love: not that we loved God but that He loved us and sent His Son as an atoning sacrifice for our sins. God made Him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him — and in Him alone! — we might become the righteousness of God. [May we never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to us and we to the world. Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. ] The only possible response to this good news is grateful repentance. Jesus who died our death invites us to live His life in the power of the Holy Spirit. This Lord who makes an everlasting covenant with us calls us to be on His side as we fight sin — in us and around us — with tears and with joy, in gratitude and in hope. It is for this new life in Christ Jesus that He strengthens us by this food and drink at His table. [How can we repay the LORD for all His goodness to us? We will lift up the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the LORD. We will fulfil our vows to the LORD in the presence of all His people.] At His table we do not only meet our Lord; we also meet one another there. As our Lord welcomes us, so we are to welcome our brothers and sisters, struggling saints as we are, and we are to do all we can to encourage them in love. Therefore, if you know of anything in your life that could be a hindrance to a brother or sister of yours to come to communion with you, you are urged to do all you can to remove such stumbling blocks. [For none of us lives to himself alone and none of us dies to himself alone. If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. So, whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord. ] The table of the Lord is for those who humbly trust in Him and seek to follow Him in repentance and obedience. Those, however, who live in self-righteousness, who place their hope in works or virtues of their own, and who do not show love to God and neighbour, have no place at the Lord's Supper unless they repent. Yet we should not be deterred by any sin and weakness which lingers within us against our will. The God of grace and mercy calls us to turn to Him and live! Let us pray: Almighty God, to whom all hearts are open, all desires known, and from whom no secrets are hidden: cleanse the thoughts of our hearts by the guidance of Your Holy Spirit, that we may perfectly love You, and worthily magnify Your holy name, through Christ our Lord. [All] Amen. NOTE: Another suggestion for a preparatory form is the introduction to the First Form for the Lord's Supper, as on page 226, up to the words "Let us now consider..." (p 228). This form can be read a week before the Lord's Supper is scheduled. It can also be read in the Communion service itself, if the form used in that service does not, in the view of Session, sufficiently stress self-examination. Its place would then be earlier in that service. There are congregational responses in this form. They are optional. For that reason they are placed between square brackets [ ]. Before the first response is due, the leader of the service can announce, in the suggested words, that the congregation is to use them. Another possibility is that they are used, but that the leader or one person designated by him read them. 1 Corinthians 11:28; 2 Corinthians 13:5 Romans 5:1; 8:1 1 Corinthians 11:27-29 1 Corinthians 11:26 Psalm 25:4, 5 Isaiah 53:5 Proverbs 3:34; 1 Peter 5:5 Psalm 130:1-4 Romans 5:6 1 John 4:9-10 2 Corinthians 5:21 Galatians 6:14 Romans 5:1 John 6:50-56; John 15:1-11; Romans 6:1-14 Psalm 116:12-14 Matthew 5:23-24 Romans 14:7-8

documents.title: Form for the Preparation of the Lord's Supper (II)
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/03 - The Lord's Supper/02 - Form for the Preparation of the Lord's Supper (II).md
documents.text: Form For The Preparation Of The Lord's Supper (II) Beloved in the Lord, as we hope to celebrate the Lord's Supper coming Sunday, it is our duty to prepare ourselves, as Paul says: "A man ought to examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup." In this self-examination each of us is faced with these questions: Do I believe that my sins are forgiven only because my Lord sacrificed Himself for me on the cross? Is it my sincere desire to love God and my neighbour, and to serve them according to God's Word? All those who, in answer to these questions, seek their refuge in Jesus Christ alone, are invited by the Lord to come with joyful praise to His table. Those who live in unbelief and sin will have to repent and seek forgiveness through our Lord Jesus Christ, otherwise they have no right to come to the table of the Lord, nor do they have part in the kingdom of God. Let us pray: Almighty God, we pray for Your grace that in the coming days we may rightly examine ourselves. Comfort us as repentant sinners and give us the assurance that we may look forward to a blessed celebration. And if any of us are not right with You, give grace and mercy, Lord, that in repentance they may change their way of life, and then join us coming Sunday in the celebration of this most glorious feast. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. 1 Corinthians 11:28

documents.title: Form for the Celebration of the Lord's Supper (I)
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/03 - The Lord's Supper/03 - Form for the Celebration of the Lord's Supper (I).md
documents.text: Form For The Celebration Of The Lord's Supper (I) Beloved in our Lord Jesus Christ, Our Saviour invites us to His table today. He Himself instituted the Holy Supper, as the apostle Paul tells us: "The Lord Jesus, on the night He was betrayed, took bread, and when He had given thanks, He broke it and said, 'This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.' In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, 'This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, whenever you drink it, in remembrance of Me.' For whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until He comes." Now if we are to celebrate this sacrament to the glory of God and the strengthening of our faith, we must first examine ourselves. This is what Scripture says: "A man ought to examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup. For anyone who eats and drinks without recognising the body of the Lord eats and drinks judgment on himself." First of all, each one of us should ask himself if he is truly sorry for his sin. Both God's Word and this sacrament remind us that God is very angry at our rebellion and disobedience. Rather than leave it unpunished, He laid it on His beloved Son, Jesus Christ, in His bitter and shameful death on the cross. Then also, let each one of us search his heart whether he believes the sure promise of God that, because of the bitter suffering and death of Christ, all his sins are now forgiven him. In faith he may appear before the holy face of God, clothed in the pure white garment of Jesus' perfect obedience, by grace freely given him as his own. Finally, let each of us examine his conscience, to see if he is truly thankful to God for His marvellous gift of redemption. Is there a true willingness to live before Him in love towards God and fellow man? Is there an earnest desire to do all the good commandments of the Lord? All those who are thus minded, God will certainly welcome as worthy partakers to this table of His Son. Those who do not have this testimony in their hearts, however, are warned in the name of the Lord. If they choose for themselves a lifestyle that excludes the Lord and do not want to repent, they should turn back to the Lord or else stay away from this table; otherwise they will eat and drink judgment to themselves and fall under heavier condemnation. God does not take pleasure in the death of the sinner but rather that he turns to Him and lives. He therefore calls you and calls all men away from the ways of death [ as He describes them in His Word: – the worship of any creatures instead of Him, the only true God; – the trust in any powers instead of or alongside our heavenly Father; – disregard for God's holy name or God's holy day, His Word or sacraments; – disobedience to parents and other God-ordained authority; – hatred, jealousy and envy as well as drunkenness and selfish misuse of God's good gifts; – sexual immorality and the denial of love and faithfulness in marriage; – the love of money and of goods and possessions; – slanderous talk, untruthful words and deceitful actions. ] Scripture says that all who walk in these ways with delight have no part in the kingdom of God. When God tells these things to those who believe in Jesus Christ, it is not in order to make them think that only the perfect can come to the table of the Lord. It is sinners, not the righteous, who are called to repentance. When we are sorry before God because of our sins and shortcomings and seek in Jesus the life we know we do not have in ourselves, God welcomes us at the table of His covenant, where He says: "I will be their God, and they will be My people." And so this very sacrament is to strengthen us in our faith and in the resolve to do battle against the sin that still remains in us and around us. It calls us to rejoice in the wonderful grace whereby the Son of God "...welcomes sinners and eats with them,"calling and enabling them to "...go and sin no more." Let us now consider the purpose for which the Lord has given us this Supper, namely that we should eat and drink it in remembrance of Him. We remember that the Lord Jesus, true God from eternity, was sent by the Father into this world to become true man. We remember that all the time He lived on earth He was burdened by our sin and God's judgment upon it. We remember that in His agony in the garden He sweated drops of blood under the weight of our sins. We remember that He was tied in bonds to set us free forever. We remember that He suffered disgrace and ridicule to give us the dignity of being children of God for ever. We remember that He, the innocent One, was condemned to death to have us, the guilty ones, acquitted at the judgment seat of God. We remember Him who took upon Himself our curse that we might be filled with His blessing. He is the One who humbled Himself into the deepest desolation and agony of hell, when on the cross He cried: "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?" This was done so that we might be welcomed by God and nevermore forsaken. We remember how He confirmed with His death and the shedding of His blood the new and eternal testament, the covenant of grace and reconciliation, when He said: "It is finished!" But we also remember that this Lord Jesus, after having suffered for us the agony of death, arose from the grave as the first-born of those who have fallen asleep, and ascended into heaven. We confess Him, ruling all things in glory and power, and as we sit around this table with the humble signs of bread broken and wine poured out, we do so in expectation of His coming again to restore all creation to praise and beauty. At this table we have communion with Him, true God and true Man. We are members by grace of His Body, saved forever from sin and assured by the Holy Spirit of the victory that overcomes the world. That Spirit, who dwells in Christ as the Head of the Church and in us as members of the Body, gives us each day the life which we may live unto God forever. And so we will not despair even when our faith is weak and our works fall so far short of God's standards, for we know that... "...He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the Day of Christ Jesus." At this table we also have communion with one another. The Holy Spirit who unites us to our Lord in glory also binds us together as believers, as the apostle says: "Because there is one loaf, we, who are many, are one body, for we all partake of the one loaf." We are one body, called to love one another from the heart, serve one another with our lives, and bear with one another in patience... "...let us encourage one another — and all the more as you see the Day approaching." Prayer: Merciful God and Father, whose grace abounds beyond all our sins, we pray that in this Supper in which we remember the bitter death of Your dear Son, You will so work in our hearts that we may yield ourselves more and more to Jesus Christ, our Saviour and our Lord. Grant that our hearts, broken in true repentance, can rejoice in Your salvation, nourished and refreshed with Him, the true heavenly Bread, through the power of the Holy Spirit. Make us so one with Him that we no longer live in our sins but in Him, and He in us. So confirm us in the covenant of Your grace that we may not doubt that You will for ever be our gracious Father, never again imputing our sins to us, and abundantly providing us, as Your dear children and heirs, with all things necessary for body and soul. Grant us Your grace, then, that we may cheerfully take up our cross, deny ourselves, confess our Saviour, and in all temptations and trials expect our Lord Jesus from heaven, who at His coming will make our temporary, earthly bodies like His glorified body, and take us to Himself in eternity. Through Him, our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom, with You and the Holy Spirit, belong all praise and adoration, now and forevermore. Amen. The congregation is requested to arise. The minister indicates which of the two creeds to use, and says: Let us now unite with the Church of all ages in the glad profession of the Faith once delivered to the saints, of which we speak with heart and mouth, saying: EITHER: APOSTLES' CREED I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth. And in Jesus Christ, His only Son, our Lord. Who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the virgin Mary; suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, dead, and buried; He descended into hell. The third day He rose again from the dead; He ascended into heaven, and is seated at the right hand of God the Father Almighty; from there He shall come to judge the living and the dead. I believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church, the communion of saints; the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and the life everlasting. Amen. OR: NICENE CREED We believe in one God, the Father almighty, maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only Son of God, begotten from the Father before all ages, God from God, Light from Light, true God from true God, begotten, not made; of the same essence as the Father. Through Him all things were made. For us and for our salvation He came down from heaven; He became incarnate by the Holy Spirit and the virgin Mary, and was made human. He was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate; He suffered and was buried. The third day He rose again, according to the Scriptures. He ascended to heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father. He will come again with glory to judge the living and the dead. His kingdom will never end. And we believe in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, the giver of life. He proceeds from the Father and the Son, and with the Father and the Son is worshipped and glorified. He spoke through the prophets. We believe in one holy catholic and apostolic church. We affirm one baptism for the forgiveness of sins. We look forward to the resurrection of the dead, and to life in the world to come. Amen. The congregation is seated. The minister then issues the invitation to communicant members and guests known to Session. While the table is prepared a psalm or hymn may be sung. At the table, the minister shall say: That we, then, may be nourished with Christ, the true Bread from heaven, let us lift our hearts to heaven, where He is, our Mediator, at the right hand of the Father. We must not doubt that we shall receive His body and blood as our food unto life eternal, through the gracious work of the Holy Spirit, as truly as we receive this bread and drink in remembrance of Him. In breaking and distributing the bread, the minister shall say: The bread which we break is the sharing of the body of Christ. Take it, eat, remember and believe that the body of our Lord Jesus Christ was given for a complete forgiveness of all our sins. In serving the cup, the minister shall say: The cup of thanksgiving for which we give thanks, is the sharing of the blood of Christ. Take it, drink from it, all of you, remember and believe that the precious blood of our Lord Jesus Christ was poured out for a complete forgiveness of all our sins. While the elements are being distributed, or for a brief period following that, the minister or another member of the congregation may read fitting passages from Scripture, or a psalm or hymn may be sung. Suggested readings for the thanksgiving at the conclusion of the day's celebration of the Lord's Supper: Psalm 36:5-10. Psalm 103:1-4; Psalm 103:8-13; Psalm 103:20-22. Romans 5:8-10; Romans 8:31-39. Revelation 4:11; Revelation 5:13. At the conclusion of the celebration the Lord's Prayer may be said in unison or the following prayer may be used: Almighty and gracious God and Father, We thank You for the Son of Your love, who, as the Shepherd dying for His sheep, became to our hungry and thirsty lives the true Food and Drink to life everlasting. We ask You to bind us to Him in ever-growing faithfulness and obedience, so that, strengthened by Your gifts of grace, we will be His witnesses at home, in the world, and to all creation. Bind us then also to all members of Christ's Body, in this church and wherever we meet them, that in love and glad use of our gifts, we may work together for Your glory. Keep us together as Your covenant people in the world, gladly bearing one another's burdens and advancing Your kingdom, until we sit with our exalted Lord at His wedding Supper, where our faith will be sight, our joy complete, and Your praise unbroken at last. Through Him, our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom with You, Father, and the Holy Spirit, the one only God, be all honour and glory for ever. Amen. The intercessions of the congregation for both local and universal needs may also be incorporated in this last prayer. In smaller congregations, this prayer of praise and intercession around the table of the Lord could be led by more than one person at the direction of the Session. 1 Corinthians 11:23-26 1 Corinthians 11:28-29. Note it says "judgment", not "condemnation". See also 2 Corinthians 13:5-6 Ezekiel 18:23; 33:11 Psalm 139:24; Proverbs 8:36; Ephesians 5:6; Galatians 5:17-21 The material between [ ] can be omitted if already covered earlier in the service, e.g., in the reading of the law. Jeremiah 31:33; 2 Corinthians 6:16 Luke 15:2 John 8:11 Galatians 4:4-5 Hebrews 5:7-9 Matthew 26:36-46 John 18:8, 12 Matthew 27:39-44 Matthew 26:65-66; John 19:11; Hebrews 9:27-28 Galatians 3:13 Matthew 27:46 John 19:30 1 John 5:4 Philippians 1:6 1 Corinthians 10:17 Hebrews 10:25 By this we understand that Christ suffered the God-forsaken agony of hell on the cross. Congregations are free to substitute this clause with having suffered the torments of Hell for liturgical use. documents.title: Form for the Celebration of the Lord's Supper (II)
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/03 - The Lord's Supper/04 - Form for the Celebration of the Lord's Supper (II).md
documents.text: Form For The Celebration Of The Lord's Supper (II) EXHORTATION Beloved in the Lord Jesus Christ, In the night before He went to the cross, "...Jesus took bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to His disciples, saying, 'Take and eat, this is My body.' Then He took the cup, gave thanks and offered it to them saying, 'Drink from it, all of you. This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. I tell you, I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father's kingdom'." God's Word commands all believers to proclaim Christ's death at this communion. Until He comes again, we are to remember Him under the signs of bread and wine, which represent His body crucified, and His blood poured out, for our sins. Thus this Supper first of all tells us that Jesus as the Good Shepherd laid down His life for the sheep. "...He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him..." At this table, we, with the hand and mouth of faith, through the mysterious work of the Holy Spirit, truly receive Christ who gave Himself on earth in the sacrifice of the cross, and now sits at the right hand of God the Father Almighty. This Supper also speaks to us of the fellowship we have with one another. It is one table around which we meet, one bread that we eat,and one wine which we drink. The Holy Spirit who unites us with our exalted Saviour, also binds us together in brotherly love. Thus, around the Lord's table we give visible expression to that Body of which He is the Head and we are the members. And so, living from forgiving grace, we extend forgiveness to one another. As He served us, we are each other's servants. As He loved us first, we love one another. As He intercedes for us, we pray for one another. Finally, the celebration of the Lord's Supper makes us look ahead with deep longing towards the Day of the Lord's coming again. In the night before His death He said that He would not eat the Passover again with His followers "until it finds fulfilment in the kingdom of God." Joyfully we confess that the promised kingdom has begun to come with power: in the glory of Christ's resurrection, His ascension into heaven, and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit. It is in that kingdom that our exalted Lord already has His supper with His Church on earth. Yet, as we struggle to make His royal claims known to a rebelling world, we eagerly await that final fulfilment when He will appear before all eyes and hand over the kingdom — completed! — to God the Father, so that God may be all in all. Thus, we celebrate the wedding feast of the Lamb here on earth as a foretaste and assurance of the perfect joy to come. "Blessed are those who are invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb!" CONFESSION OF SIN The congregation may be invited to join in. As we see the abundant grace which the Lord shows us in this Supper, it becomes even clearer to us how far we have drifted away from our God and how grievously we have broken His holy commandments, provoking His anger. We therefore do not come to this Supper to demonstrate how perfect we are in ourselves. We are straying sheep and faithless children. Therefore we cry to God: "Do not bring Your servant into judgment!" ASSURANCE OF PARDON But thanks be to God, who in boundless mercy offers forgiveness to all who sincerely repent and seek their refuge in Christ Jesus. "For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that whoever believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life." "Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life, but whoever rejects the Son will not see life, for God's wrath remains on him." In the suffering and death of Christ, not only the terrible weight of sin becomes manifest, but also the limitless extent of God's love: "For His anger lasts only a moment, but His favour lasts a lifetime!" All who trust in Jesus Christ, the Crucified and Risen, are accepted by God in grace. They may share at this table the communion with the Lord Jesus Christ and with all who in trial and persecution look with uplifted head towards the great Day of the Lord. However, all who trust in themselves for their peace with God, and those who do not repent of their sins, those who do not desire humbly to live in obedience to God and in peace with their neighbour, are urgently called to seek the newness of life which God's grace in Christ can give. Otherwise they should not come to this table lest they eat and drink judgment to themselves. Let us pray. It is our duty and delight, Lord God our Father, to give You thanks and praise for all You have done for the world. You called it into being that it should be to the praise of Your glory in everlasting life and beauty, led by man made in Your image. Then, when Your covenant partner fell and became Your enemy, leading all Your handiwork astray into death, You sent Your Son in sovereign love to redeem him and his world. We thank You that Jesus was born among us to be the Second Adam; that He lived our common life in this valley of tears Your world had become; that He suffered our sorrows and the God-forsaken agony of hell; that He died our death. But, Father, we praise You that death could not hold Him and that He now lives, ever to make intercession for us at Your right hand, yet is present with us through the Holy Spirit. We pray that the power of that Spirit may so use this Holy Supper that we may truly celebrate our union with Jesus Himself, rejoicing in His victory and strengthening each other in the hope which You have brought to this earth of Yours. We thank You with all Your saints in heaven and on earth, for this Gift which is greater than words can express, our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen. The congregation is requested to arise. The minister indicates which of the two creeds to use, and says: Let us now unite with the Church of all ages in the glad profession of the Faith once delivered to the saints, of which we speak with heart and mouth, saying: EITHER: APOSTLES' CREED I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth. And in Jesus Christ, His only Son, our Lord. Who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the virgin Mary; suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, dead, and buried; He descended into hell. The third day He rose again from the dead; He ascended into heaven, and is seated at the right hand of God the Father Almighty; from there He shall come to judge the living and the dead. I believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church, the communion of saints; the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and the life everlasting. Amen. OR: NICENE CREED We believe in one God, the Father almighty, maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only Son of God, begotten from the Father before all ages, God from God, Light from Light, true God from true God, begotten, not made; of the same essence as the Father. Through Him all things were made. For us and for our salvation He came down from heaven; He became incarnate by the Holy Spirit and the virgin Mary, and was made human. He was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate; He suffered and was buried. The third day He rose again, according to the Scriptures. He ascended to heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father. He will come again with glory to judge the living and the dead. His kingdom will never end. And we believe in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, the giver of life. He proceeds from the Father and the Son, and with the Father and the Son is worshipped and glorified. He spoke through the prophets. We believe in one holy catholic and apostolic church. We affirm one baptism for the forgiveness of sins. We look forward to the resurrection of the dead, and to life in the world to come. Amen. The congregation is seated. The minister then issues the invitation to communicant members and guests known to Session and says: Jesus Christ welcomes to the fellowship of this table all those who are sincerely sorry for their sins and renew their promise to live a godly life. So come then with glad assurance and joyful praise. A psalm or hymn of praise is sung. In congregations where the people come forward to the table, they now do so. Then the minister says: That we, then, may be nourished with Christ, the true Bread from heaven, let us lift our hearts to heaven, where He is, our Mediator, at the right hand of the Father. We must not doubt that we shall receive His body and blood as our food unto life eternal, through the gracious work of the Holy Spirit, as truly as we receive this bread and drink in remembrance of Him. In breaking and distributing the bread, the minister shall say: The bread which we break is the sharing of the body of Christ. Take it, eat, remember and believe that the body of our Lord Jesus Christ was given for a complete forgiveness of all our sins. In serving the cup, the minister shall say: The cup of thanksgiving or which we give thanks, is the sharing of the blood of Christ. Take it, drink from it, all of you, remember and believe that the precious blood of our Lord Jesus Christ was poured out for a complete forgiveness of all our sins. While the elements are being distributed, or for a brief period following that, the minister or another member of the congregation may read fitting passages from Scripture, or a psalm or hymn may be sung. Suggested readings for the thanksgiving at the conclusion of the day's celebration of the Lord's Supper: Psalm 36:5-10. Psalm 103:1-4; Psalm 103:8-13; Psalm 103:20-22. Romans 5:8-10; Romans 8:31-39. Revelation 4:11; Revelation 5:13. Prayer of thanksgiving: Heavenly Father, God of all mercy, You have set our feet on the pathway of life, through the sacrifice unto death of Jesus Christ, Your Son. When we were at our end where only hell awaited us, You made a new beginning through Him who bore our condemnation. Make us now, we pray, Your messengers of peace: willing to forgive, ready to sacrifice, patient and persistent as we extend to others Your invitation to a new and holy life. Give us the vision to see that the whole world belongs to You, and the courage to resist the false claims of the evil one. Make the message of Your great salvation reach both those who have never heard it and those who have strayed away. Lord, we look for the Day to come soon, when we shall see our Saviour no longer in the signs of broken bread and poured-out wine, but in glory coming on the clouds of heaven, to unite Your whole creation in everlasting peace and praise. Through Him, our Lord Jesus Christ, who taught us to pray: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name, Your Kingdom come, Your will be done on earth as in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. Forgive us our sins, as we forgive those who sin against us. Lead us not into temptation but deliver us from the evil one. For the kingdom, the power and the glory are Yours, now and for ever. Amen. The intercessions of the congregation for both local and universal needs may also be incorporated in this last prayer. In smaller congregations, this prayer of praise and intercession around the table of the Lord could be led by more than one person at the direction of the Session. documents.title: Form for the Celebration of the Lord's Supper (III)
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/03 - The Lord's Supper/05 - Form for the Celebration of the Lord's Supper (III).md
documents.text: Form For The Celebration Of The Lord's Supper (III) Beloved in our Lord Jesus Christ, In this service our Lord calls us to His table to have communion with Him as well as with each other. Let us listen to what the gospel tells us about the first celebration of the Lord's Supper: In the night before He went to the cross, "Jesus took bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to His disciples, saying, 'Take and eat, this is My body.' Then He took the cup, gave thanks and offered it to them, saying, 'Drink from it, all of you. This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. I tell you, I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father's kingdom'." It is the will of the Lord that all believers join in this communion. For although it is true that our sins make us unfit to come into His presence, it is just as true that Christ offered Himself as a payment for all our sins. Surely, this is what the Supper teaches us. All who trust in Jesus Christ, the Crucified and Risen, are accepted by God in grace. They may share at this table the communion with the Lord Jesus Christ and with all who, in trial and persecution, look with uplifted head towards the great Day of the Lord. However, all who trust in themselves for their peace with God, and those who do not repent of their sins, those who do not desire humbly to live in obedience to God and in peace with their neighbour, are urgently called to seek the newness of life which God's grace can give. Otherwise they should not come to this table lest they eat and drink judgment to themselves. The bread and wine represent the body and blood of the Saviour. They are received in faith as signs and seals of all the benefits of His sacrifice on the cross. The bread and wine are an illustration and guarantee to believers of the forgiveness of sins, of the strengthening of our faith, and of the communion of believers with the Lord as well as with each other. These signs and seals of the covenant of grace declare that God is faithful in fulfilling the promises of that covenant, they call upon us to live as God's children in this world and they encourage us to look forward with joy to the Day when God will be all in all. Let us pray: The congregation may be invited to join in. Merciful God, we do not come to this table trusting in our own goodness and virtue. We come because Christ has invited us. We come because we are sinful people in need of forgiveness. We come because we are hungry for life and need to be fed. Father, forgive us and feed us. We come in wonder and gratitude to offer our very selves to You in worship and adoration. Father, accept our praise, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. The minister then issues an invitation to communicant members and guests known to Session and says: Jesus Christ welcomes to the fellowship of His table all those who are sincerely sorry for their sins and who renew their promise to live a godly life. So come then with glad assurance and joyful praise. A psalm or hymn is sung. In congregations where the people come forward to the table, they now do so. The minister says: Lift up your hearts! Look to your Lord in faith! In breaking and distributing the bread, the minister shall say: The bread which we break is the sharing of the body of Christ. Take it, eat, remember and believe that the body of our Lord Jesus Christ was given for a complete forgiveness of all our sins. In serving the cup, the minister shall say: The cup of thanksgiving for which we give thanks, is the sharing of the blood of Christ. Take it, drink from it, all of you, remember and believe that the precious blood of our Lord Jesus Christ was poured out for a complete forgiveness of all our sins. While the elements are being distributed, or for a brief period following that, the minister may read fitting passages from Scripture, or a psalm or hymn may be sung. Suggested readings for the thanksgiving at the conclusion of the day's celebration of the Lord's Supper: Psalm 36:5-10. Psalm 103:1-4; Psalm 103:8-13; Psalm 103:20-22. Romans 5:8-10; Romans 8:31-39. Revelation 4:11; Revelation 5:13. Prayer of thanksgiving. The congregation may be invited to join in. EITHER: For the bread that we have eaten, for the wine that we have tasted, for the life that You have given, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, we will praise You! For the life of Christ within us, turning all our fears to freedom helping us to live for others: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, we will praise You! For the strength of Christ to lead us in our living and our dying, in the end with all Your people: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, we will praise You! Amen. OR: Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, we bring You glory, thanks and praise, for all that we have seen and heard, tasted and handled, of the Word of Life; for the fellowship with You and with Your Son, and with all Your people, too. We humbly ask You, to accept us as we dedicate ourselves to You — again. Help us with Your daily grace, that we may continue in this fellowship, that our hearts may be filled with new courage and hope; that we may live to Your glory. Through Jesus Christ, our Lord. Amen. Matthew 26:26-29 1 Corinthians 11:27-29 Or: communion Or: remission Or: blessing Or: communion Or: shed Or: remission

documents.title: Form for the Celebration of the Lord's Supper (IV)
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/03 - The Lord's Supper/06 - Form for the Celebration of the Lord's Supper (IV).md
documents.text: Form For The Celebration Of The Lord's Supper (IV) M Brothers and sisters in Christ, the gospels tell us that on the first day of the week, the day on which our Lord rose from the dead, He appeared to some of His disciples and was made known to them in the breaking of the bread. Come, then, to the joyful feast of the Lord. THE THANKSGIVING Lift up your hearts! C We lift them up to the Lord! M Let us give thanks to the Lord our God. C It is right for us to give thanks, it is our joy and our peace, at all times and in all places to give thanks to You, holy Father, almighty, everlasting God, through Christ our Lord. M We bless You for Your continual love and care for every creature. We praise You for forming us in Your image and calling us to be Your people. We thank You that You did not abandon us in our rebellion against Your love, but sent prophets and teachers to lead us into the way of salvation. Above all we thank You for sending Jesus Your Son to deliver us from the way of sin and death by the obedience of His life, by His suffering upon the cross, and by His resurrection from the dead. We praise You that He now reigns with You in glory and ever lives to pray for us. We thank You for the Holy Spirit who leads us into truth, defends us in adversity, and out of every people unites us into one holy Church. Therefore with the whole company of saints in heaven and on earth we worship and glorify You, God most holy, and we sing with joy: C Holy, holy, holy! Lord God almighty! all Thy works shall praise Thy name, in earth and sky and sea; holy, holy, holy! Merciful and mighty, God in three Persons, blessed Trinity! THE INSTITUTION M We give thanks to God the Father that our Saviour, Jesus Christ, before He suffered, gave us this sign and seal of His sacrifice, until His coming again. For "the Lord Jesus, on the night He was betrayed, took bread, and when He had given thanks, He broke it and said, 'This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.' In the same way, after supper, He took the cup, saying, 'This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, whenever you drink it, in remembrance of Me.' For whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until He comes." C We shall do as our Lord commands. We proclaim that our Lord Jesus was sent by the Father into the world, that He took upon Himself our flesh and blood, that He bore the wrath of God against our sin. We confess that He was condemned to die that we might be pardoned, and suffered death that we might live. We proclaim that He is risen to make us right with God, and that He shall come again in the glory of His new creation. This we do now and until He comes again. PRAYER OF CONSECRATION M Heavenly Father, Through this sacrament, show forth among us the presence of Your life-giving Word and Holy Spirit, to sanctify us and Your whole Church. Give that all who share the body and blood of our Saviour Jesus Christ may be one in Him, and remain faithful in love and hope. And, as these many grains have been gathered into one loaf, and these many grapes into one cup, grant, O Lord, that Your whole Church may soon be gathered from the ends of the earth into Your kingdom. Now, as our Saviour Christ has taught us, we pray: C Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name, Your Kingdom come, Your will be done on earth as in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. Forgive us our sins, as we forgive those who sin against us. Lead us not into temptation but deliver us from the evil one. For the kingdom, the power and the glory are Yours, now and for ever. Amen. As the minister breaks the bread and pours the wine: M The bread which we break is a sharing in the body of Christ. C We who are many are one body, for we all share the same loaf. M The cup for which we give thanks is a sharing in the blood of Christ. C The cup from which we drink is our participation in the blood of Christ. THE INVITATION The following invitation is for communicant members and guests known to Session. This should have been made plain in the church bulletin or by way of announcement before the service, so that the words of the invitation are not misunderstood. The naming of the guests can take place at the point indicated below by the asterisk (). M Congregation in the Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord has prepared His table for all who love Him and trust in Him alone for their salvation. All who are truly sorry for their sins, who sincerely believe in the Lord Jesus as their Saviour, and who desire to live in obedience to Him, are now invited to come with gladness to the table of the Lord. All those, however, who do not have this faith and repentance in their hearts, but who live in wilful disobedience to the Lord, are urged to turn from these ways of rebellion, or — if not — to stay away from this food and drink which Christ has ordained for His people, lest they eat and drink judgment on themselves. THE DEDICATION C Holy Father, in thanks for the sacrifice of Your Son, Jesus Christ, in the joy of His resurrection, in the hope of His coming again, we present ourselves a living sacrifice and come to the table of our Lord. M indicating the elements: The gifts of God for the people of God. THE COMMUNION When the people are ready to eat the bread: Take, eat, remember and believe that the body of our Lord Jesus Christ was given for a complete forgiveness of all our sins. When the people are ready to drink from the cup: Take, drink, remember and believe that the precious blood of our Lord Jesus Christ was given for a complete forgiveness of all our sins. THE THANKSGIVING Congregation in Christ, since the Lord has fed us at His table, let us praise His holy name with thanksgiving. C Praise the LORD, O my soul; all my inmost being, praise His holy name. Praise the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all His benefits — who forgives all your sins and heals all your diseases, who redeems your life from the pit and crowns you with love and compassion, who satisfies your desires with good things!... For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is His love for those who fear Him; as far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us. As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear Him. Praise the LORD, O my soul!1 Therefore shall my mouth and heart show forth the praise of the LORD, from this time onward for evermore. Amen. A psalm or hymn may be sung. M = Minister Luke 24:30-31, 35 C = Congregation, in unison Book of Worship hymn 164:4, to be sung without prelude 1 Corinthians 11:23-26 Romans 4:25 1 Corinthians 11:27-29 Romans 12:1 Psalm 103:1-5a; 11-13; 22b

documents.title: Form for the Celebration of the Lord's Supper (V)
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/03 - The Lord's Supper/07 - Form for the Celebration of the Lord's Supper (V).md
documents.text: Form For The Celebration Of The Lord's Supper (V) M The Lord be with you C The Lord be with you also. M Lift up your hearts! C We lift them up to the Lord! M Let us give thanks to the Lord. C He is worthy to be praised. M Truly it is fitting, it is our joy and happiness to give thanks to You, almighty Father, eternal God, through Jesus Christ, our Lord. He took the form of man. He humbled Himself to death, even the death of the cross. Therefore, You have highly exalted Him and given Him the name that is above every name, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth, to the glory of God the Father. Therefore, with the glorified Church and all the company of heaven, we praise You, as we sing with joy: C Holy, holy, holy! Lord God almighty! all Thy works shall praise Thy name, in earth and sky and sea; holy, holy, holy! Merciful and mighty, God in three Persons, blessed Trinity! THE INSTITUTION M In the night in which He was betrayed, our Lord Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it and said, "This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me." In the same way, after supper, He took the cup, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood, do this, whenever you drink it, in remembrance of Me." C So we remember the redeeming sufferings of the Messiah, our Lord, who rose again and lives. We will proclaim His death till He comes. Maranatha! M Let us pray. Prayer Merciful God and Father, we humbly ask You, that in this Supper, in which we cherish the blessed memory of the bitter death of Your Son, Jesus Christ, You will so work in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, that we, with true confidence, surrender more and more to Your Son Jesus Christ, in order that our burdened and contrite hearts, through the power of the Holy Spirit, may be nourished and refreshed with His true body and blood, yes, with Him who is truly God and man, the only heavenly bread; and that we may no longer live in our sins, but He in us and we in Him, and so truly be partakers of the new and everlasting testament, the covenant of grace, that we do not doubt that You will forever be our gracious Father, never again holding our sins against us, and providing us as Your dear children and heirs with all we need for body and soul. Hear us, O God and merciful Father, through Jesus Christ, in whose name we pray with all Your children together: C Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name, Your Kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. Forgive us our sins, as we forgive those who sin against us. Lead us not into temptation but deliver us from the evil one. For the kingdom, the power and the glory are Yours, now and for ever. Amen. AGNUS DEI (Lamb of God) All sing: O Lamb of God most holy! Who on the cross did languish; e'er patient, meek and lowly, though mocked amid Your anguish; all sin You have borne for us, else would despair reign o'er us; have mercy on us, O Jesus! Your peace be with us, O Jesus! THE INVITATION The following invitation is for communicant members and guests known to Session. This should have been made plain in the church bulletin or by way of announcement before the service, so that the words of the invitation are not misunderstood. The naming of the guests can take place at the point indicated below by the asterisk (). M Congregation in the Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord has prepared His table for all who love Him and trust in Him alone for their salvation. All who are truly sorry for their sins, who sincerely believe in the Lord Jesus as their Saviour, and who desire to live in obedience to Him, are now invited to come with gladness to the table of the Lord. All those, however, who do not have this faith and repentance in their hearts, but who live in wilful disobedience to the Lord, are urged to turn from these ways of rebellion, or — if not — to stay away from this food and drink which Christ has ordained for His people, lest they eat and drink judgment on themselves. Come then, for all things are now ready. THE COMMUNION When the people are ready to eat the bread: Take, eat, remember and believe that the body of our Lord Jesus Christ was given for a complete forgiveness of all our sins. When the people are ready to drink from the cup: Take, drink, remember and believe that the precious blood of our Lord Jesus Christ was given for a complete forgiveness of all our sins. THE THANKSGIVING Congregation in Christ, since the Lord has fed us at His table, let us praise His holy name with thanksgiving. C Praise the LORD, O my soul; all my inmost being, praise His holy name. Praise the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all His benefits — who forgives all your sins and heals all your diseases, who redeems your life from the pit and crowns you with love and compassion, who satisfies your desires with good things!... For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is His love for those who fear Him; as far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us. As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear Him. Praise the LORD, O my soul! Therefore shall my mouth and heart show forth the praise of the LORD, from this time onward for evermore. Amen. A psalm or hymn may be sung. M = Minister C = Congregation, in unison Philippians 2:7-11 Book of Worship hymn 164:4, to be sung without prelude 1 Corinthians 11:23-26 The word "Maranatha!" which occurs in older translations of 1 Corinthians 16:22, can mean three things: "The Lord has come", "The Lord is coming", and the prayer we find in the NIV: "O Lord, come!". This prayer is based on that of the classic Form which, originating from Calvin, received its basic shape in the Palatinate, where the Heidelberg Catechism was written. Olevianus was also one of the authors of this Form. It has been used in Reformed churches all over the world for centuries. Book of Worship hymn 298:1, to be sung unannounced, without prelude 1 Corinthians 11:27-29 Psalm 103:1-5a; 11-13; 22b

documents.title: Public Exhortations re Communicant Members
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/04 - Discipline/01 - Public Exhortations re Communicant Members.md
documents.text: Discipline: Public Exhortations Re Communicant Members FIRST PUBLIC ADMONITION OF CHRISTIAN DISCIPLINE It is the sad duty of your Session to inform you that one of our brothers/sisters, a communicant member, has for some time already been barred from the Lord's table because of his/her un-Christian life. Despite urgent and repeated warnings by the office bearers, we found no evidence of repentance. We now have to inform you that this member of our church is in grave spiritual danger and if he/she does not turn back to the Lord, we may ultimately have to excommunicate him/her. Making this known to you for the first time, we plead with you to remember in your prayers all the covenant members who are backsliding, and especially those in our fellowship. May our gracious Lord and Saviour hear our prayers. SECOND PUBLIC ADMONITION OF CHRISTIAN DISCIPLINE As you will remember, some years/months ago, we informed you that one of our members had to be barred from the Lord's table because of his/her un-Christian life. We have prayed, we have pleaded and lovingly admonished, but all our efforts so far were in vain. This brother/sister has consistently refused to listen to the church. He/she has not yet shown repentance. In obedience to the Word of the Lord we must now proceed. We have asked the advice of the churches in our Classis and were told that we should inform our congregation and announce the name of the brother/sister concerned. His/her name is Full Name of Address . We urge you to pray for him/her and, if at all possible, to visit him/her and to plead with him/her in love and compassion to return to the obedience and joy of our Lord and Saviour. If he/she refuses to listen and to repent, your Session will need to excommunicate him/her from our church and declare that he/she can no longer be a member of God's kingdom. THIRD PUBLIC ADMONITION OF CHRISTIAN DISCIPLINE Session informed you some time ago that Full Name of Address is living an un-Christian life, for which reason we had to bar him/her from the Lord's table. We also told you that unless true repentance was shown we would have to proceed with Christian discipline. We have now come to the sad conclusion that he/she has hardened his/her heart and appears to be an unbeliever. Let us all pray fervently during this week that it may please the Lord to work mightily in the heart of Full Name . If we find no evidence of repentance during this week, we will have to proceed with discipline, and next Sunday exclude him/her from the fellowship of the church by public excommunication and declare that he/she can no longer be a member of the kingdom of God. May the Lord in His great mercy hear our prayers. This first admonition can be given at the discretion of Session. For the subsequent two admonitions, which involve the naming the delinquent, the concurrence of the Classis is required. Galatians 6:1-2; Luke 15:7, 10; Psalm 51:12, 17 1 Corinthians 5:1-5, 13; 6:9-10

documents.title: Form for Excommunication
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/04 - Discipline/02 - Form for Excommunication.md
documents.text: Discipline: Form for Excommunication Beloved in the Lord Jesus Christ. It is known to you that, from time to time, we have made announce-ments concerning our brother/sister Full Name . His/her life has given us concern and we have had reason to question his/her standing in God's covenant and church. You were asked several times to pray for him/her and, in brotherly love, to urge him/her to return from his/her way of death and repent before the Lord his/her God. However, no evidence of such repentance has been brought before us. Therefore the Session of this church, having heard the advice of the Classis, does now have the sad duty to proceed with his/her excommunication. We do this because Christ commanded it: "...if he refuses to listen even to the church, treat him as you would a pagan...I tell you the truth, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven." This is also clearly taught by the apostle Paul. He warns that the wilful toleration of evil in the church dishonours God and endangers His people.Clearly he instructs the church at Corinth that the wicked person must be expelled from their midst. In Christ's name he charged the elders at Ephesus to guard the flock from those appearing to be wolves, even when they arose from their own community. All Scripture clearly teaches that discipline is to safeguard God's church from disobedience, pollution and temptation, both in doctrine and life. In this way the glory and majesty of God are to be upheld in the midst of His people. At least as strongly, however, God's Word tells us that the loving aim of harsh measures is to drive sinners back to repentance. In God's own stern dealings with His disobedient people we always hear His pleading call to return to Him: "As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign LORD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that they turn from their ways and live. Turn! Turn from your evil ways! Why will you die, O house of Israel?" Even at the point that we must declare someone excluded from the church and kingdom of God, we — on God's behalf — are to call him/her to return from his/her ways and find life. According to the command of God, you, members of this church, are to extend this urgent call of love to him/her. However, you must not give him/her the privilege of teaching you or the opportunity to lead you. You cannot give him/her the kind of fellowship that would be a sharing of faith, because that would be compromising the truth of God's Word and give him/her a false sense of security. Rather, we must pray fervently to our Lord, that He will bring him/her to repentance and life. We are also called to take heed that, as we think we stand firm, we shall not fall ourselves.In this we all are made aware again of our own need of the saving and preserving grace of Jesus Christ through His Holy Spirit. Finally, as a church of Jesus Christ, we must deeply humble ourselves before the Lord our God. We mourn and grieve that the bond of love among us has not prevented our brother/sister from straying away. As we take the step of excommunication in obedience to the command of God, it is in a deep sense of our own shortcomings and weaknesses. We know that we must watch and pray so that we will not fall into temptation. The congregation is requested to stand, after which the minister shall say: In the name and authority of Jesus Christ, we, as servants and overseers of His church at this place, declare that we excommunicate Full Name from the church and declare that he/she can no longer be regarded as a member of the kingdom of God, unless he/she repents. So long as he/she persists obstinately in his/her rebellion against the revealed will of God, he/she is excluded from the fellowship of Christ, from the holy sacraments and from all the spiritual blessings and privileges which God promises and gives to His church and kingdom. To Him be the glory. Amen. The congregation is seated. Prayer: Righteous God and merciful Father. We appear before Your high and holy majesty in fear and trembling, knowing that we, every single one of us, have grievously sinned against Your holy will. We confess that we, by our own disobedience, have made ourselves worthy of being banished from the light of Your face forever. On this sad day for our congregation we come to You in humble repentance. O Lord, do not enter into judgment with Your servants. Receive us into Your grace only for the sake of Jesus Christ, our Saviour. We earnestly ask You, O Lord, that You will remove and keep far from our hearts the pride that exalts itself above other sinners. Only Your infinite mercy can keep our own feet on the way of life. Lord, we plead that mercy alone, when we now pray for Full Name who was excommunicated today from Your church and kingdom. You Yourself commanded us to do this. You know how we have sought to restore him/her to full submission to Your will. You have heard us plead with him/her to come back to joyful obedience to Your law of gratitude. We saw no signs of this but only hardness of heart. O God, again we pray to You that You will yet change his/her heart and bring him/her back to You in repentance unto life, so that there will be the joy of feasting in the house of his/her Father. For the sake of the blood of Jesus, O Lord, forgive us the shortcomings that have marred our work with this brother/sister. Forgive us the way in which we, as a congregation, may have contributed to his/her error. Create in our hearts a greater concern over him/her as well as others who might be in danger. Give us the grace not to be faithless in our dealings with one another. Grant, O merciful God and Father, that, as we mourn now over this man/woman, we may one day rejoice over him/her with the very angels in heaven, through Him, Our Lord Jesus Christ, who taught us, thus to pray: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name, Your Kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. Forgive us our sins, as we forgive those who sin against us. Lead us not into temptation but deliver us from the evil one. For the kingdom, the power and the glory are Yours, now and for ever. Amen. Matthew 18:17-18 1 Corinthians 5; 11:17-32; Ephesians 5:3-7 1 Corinthians 5:13 Acts 20:29-31. See also Joshua 7, Acts 5 and Titus 3:10 2 Corinthians 6:14-7:1; Hebrews 12:28-29 See what Paul did in 1 Corinthians 5:5 ...and why Ezekiel 33:11. See also Hosea 6:1-7 and 11:1-11 Jude 23 2 John 10 Romans 16:17-18; 1 Timothy 1:20 2 Thessalonians 3:6, 14-15; 1 Corinthians 5:11 1 Corinthians 10:12 Jude 24 Matthew 26:41; 1 Peter 5:8-9 Luke 15:22-24 Luke 15:7, 10

documents.title: Public Announcement for the Re-Admission of Excommunicated Persons
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/04 - Discipline/03 - Public Announcement for the Re-Admission of Excommunicated Persons.md
documents.text: Discipline: Public Announcement for the Re-Admission of Excommunicated Persons Beloved in the Lord. It is known to you that some time ago our fellow member Full Name of Address was excommunicated from the Church of Jesus Christ. It is our great joy to be able to announce to you now that the Lord has heard our prayers, blessed our warnings, and led this brother/sister to repentance. Full Name has now requested to be re-admitted to the fellowship of the church. Session has heard his/her testimony and is satisfied that, as there had been grounds to declare this brother/sister bound because of his/her sin, now there are grounds to declare him/her released, according to the command of Christ. We therefore intend to receive him/her again into the full communion of the church when we hope to celebrate the Lord's Supper on Date , unless any of you, in the meantime, should have valid reasons why this ought not to be done, of which you must give notice in due time. Meanwhile, let everyone thank the Lord for His grace shown this brother/sister, and pray that the Lord will continue and complete His work begun in him/her. To be read at least two Sundays before the proposed date of re-admission. If it is helpful, the time lapsed may be mentioned here, e.g., two years ago. Matthew 16:19; John 20:23 Psalm 138:8; Philippians 1:6

documents.title: Form for the Re-Admission of Excommunicated Persons
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/04 - Discipline/04 - Form for the Re-Admission of Excommunicated Persons.md
documents.text: Discipline: Form for the Re-Admission of Excommunicated Persons After the sermon, the minister shall say: Congregation of our Lord Jesus Christ. We have previously announced to you the gladdening news of the conversion of our brother/sister Full Name who has been excommunicated from the Church of Jesus Christ. We have not received any valid objection against his/her re-admission to full communion with the church. Therefore, in the name of the Lord and with great joy, we shall now proceed to do this. Our sovereign Lord says in His Word, "I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that they turn from their ways and live." Our Lord Jesus Christ, the great Shepherd, gave His life for His sheep and became the Door that they might find life and abundance. He tells of the joy in heaven even over one sinner who repents. So also Paul says, "If anyone has caused grief, ...you ought to forgive and comfort him, so that he will not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow. I urge you, therefore, to re-affirm your love for him." The Lord Jesus who said that "whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven" also assured us that "whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven." We therefore were given authority to assure anyone who truly repents of sin that he should not doubt that God accepted him in grace: "If you forgive anyone his sins, they are forgiven." Now that it may be clear to us all that you, brother/sister Full Name are returning to the profession of your faith and love towards your Lord in true repentance, you are requested to arise and to answer the following questions: 1. Do you declare with all your heart, here before God and His church, that you are sincerely sorry for the sin and error that had caused your estrangement from God and His church? 2. Do you also truly believe that the Lord God Himself, for the sake of Jesus Christ, has forgiven you and still forgives you all your sins, and has restored you into fellowship with Him? 3. Is it therefore your desire to be re-admitted to the Church of Jesus Christ and to full communion with this congregation? Do you promise by the grace of God to live according to His will, both in doctrine and in conduct, faithful to Jesus your Lord in life and in death? Full Name , what is your answer? Answer: By the grace of God, with all my heart, I do. The whole congregation shall arise and the minister shall say: We then, being here assembled in the name and authority of Jesus Christ, declare you, Full Name , to be absolved from the bonds of excommunication. We receive you again into the church of the Lord. We declare unto you that you stand in the communion of Christ, of the holy sacraments, and of all the spiritual blessings and privileges which God promises and gives to those in His church and kingdom. May our eternal God preserve you in this to the glorious Day of His Son Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory, now and for ever. All say: Amen! Then, while all remain standing, the minister shall continue with the following charges: Be assured in your heart, dear brother/sister, that the Lord Himself has received you in grace. In all your thoughts, words and actions, do not cease to praise Him for the great love He gave you. Be watchful against the wiles of Satan and the wickedness of the world, that you may not fall again into sin. Seek earnestly the fellowship of your brothers and sisters, that you may not lack strengthening and encouragement. Love Christ, for much has been forgiven you. To the congregation: And you, beloved Christians, receive this brother/sister of yours with love from the heart. "...Celebrate and be glad, because he/she was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found." Rejoice with the angels in heaven over this sinner who has come to repentance. Count him/her no longer as a foreigner and alien but as a fellow citizen with God's people and a member of God's household. A psalm or hymn may be sung, followed by prayer: Almighty God and merciful Father. We humbly thank and praise Your name! You have graciously heard our prayers. You have given life where there was death, repentance where there was rebellion, and joy where there was grief and mourning. We acknowledge that it was Your goodness alone which has brought back our brother/sister to the fold of Your people. It was the powerful working of Your Word and Spirit, and Your sovereign use also of frail human means. To Your name be praise and glory, O Shepherd of Your people, O God of all grace! We now humbly ask You that You will continue Your work in the heart of this our brother/sister. May he/she walk with You all the days of his/her life, praising Your goodness and resisting the evil one, who, as You promised, will then flee from him/her. Make him/her able, in turn, to warn and help others in the struggle against evil. So restore to him/her the joy of Your salvation, that he/she will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners will turn back to You. Grant him/her thus, finally, with all Your redeemed children, on the Day of Christ, to receive the crown of glory that will never fade away. Through Him, our Lord Jesus Christ, who with You and the Holy Spirit, one only God, lives and reigns forever. Amen. Here the service continues with the celebration of the Lord's Supper. (Form V is recommended for this occasion.) documents.text: Discipline: Baptised Members Living in Unbelief and Sin 1. ANNOUNCEMENT OF A TRIAL PERIOD FOR AN UNFAITHFUL BAPTISED MEMBER Session has the sad duty to make known to you that Full Name of Address , who is a baptised member of our church, has been continually living an un-Christian life. All our warnings and admonitions have been ignored, and we had to inform him/her that unless there is evidence of repentance in the next three months, we will have to sever his/her relationship with our church. We urge you to pray for him/her and to speak to him/her in love, reminding him/her of God's covenant promises of which he/she received the sign and seal. 2. ANNOUNCEMENT OF ERASURE OF A BAPTISED MEMBER Session has to inform you with sorrow that Full Name of Address , has not given evidence of repentance since you were informed some months ago of his/her un-Christian life. Because of his/her refusal to live in the covenant in which he/she was included, we have to sever his/her relationship with this church. Let us pray for him/her and admonish him/her in Christian love. And let us all be aware of the danger that we, too, may fall away from the living God by loving this present world.
