documents.text: Discipline: Resignation, Erasure and Re-Admission of Communicant Members 1. ANNOUNCEMENT OF RESIGNATION OF A COMMUNICANT MEMBER With sadness, we have to announce that Full Name , who used to be a communicant member of this congregation, has informed us that he/she no longer wants to belong to our church. We pray that by the grace of the Holy Spirit, by our prayers and by our loving admonition, he/she may return one day into our fellowship. 2. ANNOUNCEMENT OF ERASURE OF A COMMUNICANT MEMBER With sadness, we have to announce that Full Name , who despite much encouragement has ceased for a long time now to show interest in the life of the church, will be erased from the roll of this church in weeks' time unless a change of heart is obvious. We urge you to pray for him/her and speak to him/her. 3. ANNOUNCEMENT OF RESIGNED OR ERASED PERSON REQUESTING RE-ADMITTANCE AS A COMMUNICANT MEMBER With gratitude and joy we inform you that Full Name who had resigned / was erased as a member of our church, has requested to be accepted again into full communion. Session has granted this request and we now urge you to receive this brother/sister with love, praising God for His gracious guidance and faithfulness.

documents.title: Form for the Ordination and Installation of Office Bearers
documents.groupTitle: Ordination and Installation of Office Bearers
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/05 - Ordination and Installation of Office Bearers/01 - Form for the Ordination and Installation of Office Bearers.md
documents.text: Form For The Ordination / Installation Of Office Bearers GENERAL INTRODUCTION Congregation of our Lord Jesus Christ. Today we rejoice that God graciously maintains the special offices in His church. We thank God for those who have worked as office bearers amongst us and praise Him for providing others. On two earlier occasions the Session announced that Names have been called to the office of minister/elder/deacon in this church. Seeing that no one has raised any lawful objections against their doctrine or life, we shall now, in the name of the Lord, proceed with their ordination/ installation. Let us first listen to what the Word of God teaches regarding these offices. Christ Himself, through His Word and Spirit, gathers, protects and preserves His church but in all this He uses the services of His people. The Lord is especially pleased to work through the members of His body, the church. All are called to be prophets, priests and kings with Him, but to some He has entrusted special tasks. The apostle Paul states that Christ appointed "some to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists, and some to be pastors and teachers, to prepare God's people for works of service, so that the body of Christ may be built up until we all reach unity in the faith and in the knowledge of the Son of God and become mature, attaining to the whole measure of the fullness of Christ." In the office bearers and the work they are called to do, we see the love of Christ for His people. By His Spirit the Lord equips those who fill the offices for their tasks and through them enables the members of the church to grow in faith, develop mature Christian lives, serve others in selfless love, and share with all people the good news of salvation. Christ taught the spirit of biblical leadership when He said: "Whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wants to be first must be your slave — just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life to be a ransom for many." Office bearers, therefore, in all humility are to be servants of Christ and His people. Yet, they should do their work with the authority and dignity of Christ whom they represent. Jesus said, "I tell you the truth, whoever accepts anyone I send accepts Me; and whoever accepts Me accepts the One who sent Me." PARTICULAR OFFICES 1. Ministers of the Word Since the days of the apostles, God has called men to be ministers of the Word. This office is not higher or lower than that of elder or deacon, but each office has its own special tasks. Ministers are also elders of the church but their work is especially in preaching and teaching. God commands them to "preach the Word, be prepared in season and out of season; correct, rebuke, encourage — with great patience and careful instruction ...keep your head in all situations, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, discharge all the duties of your ministry." Such preaching has the two-fold object of calling upon sinners to be reconciled with God through Jesus Christ, and nurturing believers in the faith and life of the Kingdom of God. Whilst all believers are called upon to speak up for God, ministers of the Word especially are to be seen as Christ's ambassadors, as though God were making His appeal through them, "be reconciled with God." Therefore the ministers of the Word are to see the faithful proclamation of the Word as their first responsibility. The execution of this task calls for a diligent and humble study of the Word of God. The ministry of the Word includes the preaching of the gospel to the congregation gathered for worship, the instruction in sound doctrine, especially of covenant youth and others who are yet to profess their faith in Jesus Christ. Ministers are also called to proclaim the gospel to those outside the Christian church in order that the elect of God may be brought to Christ. To this end ministers shall teach the members of the church to be faithful witnesses. It also involves encouraging and admonishing, through the Word, the members of the church when they are visited in their homes. In all this the minister of the Word shall build up the church in the faith and knowledge of the Lord Jesus Christ. As a good shepherd watching over the sheep, he will challenge and resist the claims of the devil and refute false doctrine. He will call those who have sinned to repentance and faith. To this end ministers shall also see to it that public prayer is said on behalf of all people and those who rule over them, so that "we may live peaceful and quiet lives in all godliness and holiness." According to the command of Christ, ministers shall administer the sacraments, Baptism and the Lord's Supper, which have been instituted as signs and seals of God's covenant with His people. Ministers shall be pastors to the Lord's people. With the Word and in prayer they shall comfort those who sorrow, rejoice with those who rejoice, strengthen the weak, visit the lonely, elderly and sick, and promote the biblical foundations of the Christian home and marriage. Together with the elders, ministers shall exercise Christian oversight in the congregation and maintain good order and discipline. According to the command of Christ the keys of the kingdom are to be used faithfully so that "whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven." From all this it is clear that the ministry of the Word is a most responsible task which none can do in their own strength. Therefore we look to our faithful Saviour and Lord Jesus Christ who is able to equip His servants for the work to which He has called them. Ministers themselves must also be devoted to prayer and the reading of the Scriptures for their own edification. They must be continually filled with the Holy Spirit, watch their life and doctrine closely, and fan into flame the gift of God which is in them. So we rejoice that in His faithful love the Lord has provided us with a minister to serve as a pastor and teacher. 2. Elders The office of elder has been in existence since the days of the apostles. Elders were appointed in every church. This office is not higher or lower than that of ministers or deacons but each office has its own special tasks. The Word of God urges respect for the office of elder, and distinguishes between elders who labour particularly in preaching and teaching through the ministry of the Word, and elders who are charged with the supervision over the church.The elders of the church in Ephesus were called to keep watch over all the flock of which the Holy Spirit had made them overseers and shepherds of the church of God. Elders are therefore to rule over the church in the name of Christ, the Head and King of the church. This implies that elders are responsible for the spiritual well-being of all members under their supervision. For this reason the elders shall faithfully visit the members of the church and discuss with them the privileges and responsibilities of serving Christ. Elders shall have proper respect for the body of Christ and encourage the members to attend faithfully to the means of grace, the proclamation of the Word and participation in the sacraments. Elders are to admonish those who do not live in true fellowship with the Lord and, lovingly and patiently, call the stubborn and impenitent to repentance, using the means of Christian discipline where necessary. Elders are called to provide for true preaching and teaching, carefully supervising the ministry of the Word and the sacraments, maintaining the public worship of the holy name of God, for the purpose of building up the church of God in the knowledge and love of Christ.They are to safeguard the church against false teachings. To do all this the elders shall study God's Word diligently and prayerfully so that they themselves, as good servants of Jesus Christ, grow in knowledge and experience of the truth of the faith and of good teaching. Elders are also to extend the invitation of the gospel to the unsaved and through their own example as faithful witnesses urge the members of the church to be active in evangelism. To this end elders are to promote fellowship and hospitality among believers. Furthermore, elders shall maintain good order and decorum in the church and all its assemblies. In all matters of doctrine and conduct they shall exercise supervision over one another, for God is not a God of disorder but of peace. From all this it is clear that the office of elder is a most responsible task and no one can do it in his own strength. Therefore we look to our faithful Saviour and Lord Jesus Christ who is able to equip His servants for the work to which He has called them. Elders themselves must also be devoted to prayer and the reading of the Scriptures for their own edification. They must be continually filled with the Holy Spirit, watch their life and doctrine closely, and fan into flame the gift of God which is in them. So we rejoice that in His faithful love the Lord has provided us with elders to watch over His people. 3. Deacons The office of deacon can be traced back to the time of the apostles when they appointed suitable members of the church to provide relief for the needy. Whilst they were not yet called deacons, it is apparent that in time the office of deacon became a permanent institution in the church of God. This office is not higher or lower than that of ministers or elders, but each office has its own special tasks. The Scriptures clearly indicate that the Lord has regard for those who cry out and for the afflicted who have no one to help them. He takes pity on the weak and needy. Christ Himself has compassion on the hungry and the thirsty, the stranger and the poor, the sick and the prisoner, and those who come to their aid are seen as doing this work for Christ. Therefore deacons are to express Christ's love through the ministry of mercy. The work of deacons shall be governed by a spirit of compassion and kindness, love and cheerfulness. They shall stimulate relief in Christ's name for victims of poverty and distress, injustice and oppression. To this end deacons shall encourage the congregation to take an active part in the ministry of mercy and support the diaconate with generous giving and prayer. Deacons are to promote faithful stewardship of the riches the Lord has given His people, urge them to practice hospitality, and to develop, where necessary, programs of assistance. In the collection and disbursement of gifts required for their ministry, deacons shall act with integrity, discretion and wisdom, comforting those whom they help with the Word of God and prayer. The task of deacons is to "do good to all people, especially to those who belong to the family of believers," always being ready to defend the rights of Him who is the Father to the fatherless and the Defender of widows. Because life in God's creation is imperfect and bears the marks of the fall into sin, the reality of suffering is amongst us, but deacons may point all sufferers to Christ who knew what suffering was because He took up our infirmities and carried our sorrows. Deacons may comfort all believers who are afflicted by reminding them of the perfection of the kingdom of heaven in which, when it shall be fully established at Christ's coming, "God will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the old order of things has passed away." In their ministry of compassion, deacons shall rekindle in God's people the hope of things to come and remind them that: "our present sufferings are not worth comparing with the glory that shall be revealed in us." From all this it is clear that the office of deacon is a most responsible task and no one can do it in his own strength. Therefore we look to our faithful Saviour and Lord Jesus Christ who is able to equip His servants for the work to which He has called them. Deacons themselves must also be devoted to prayer and the reading of the Scriptures for their own edification. They must be continually filled with the Holy Spirit, watch their life and doctrine closely, and fan into flame the gift of God which is in them. So we rejoice that in His faithful love the Lord has provided us with deacons to help us be a merciful and compassionate people. VOWS Names , to express your acceptance of the office of Minister of the Word/Elder/Deacon, you are asked to stand, and here in the presence of God and His church to answer the following questions: 1. Do you believe that, in the call of this congregation, you are being called by God Himself to serve in this holy office / these holy offices? 2. Do you believe that the Scriptures of the Old and New Testament are the Word of God and that in them the way of salvation is taught completely, and do you accept the confessional standards of the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia as being in harmony with the Scriptures? Do you promise to defend this gospel and to reject all teachings that contradict it; to speak against all injustice and all untruth, and model for this congregation God's concern for compassion, justice and peace? 3. Do you promise to carry out the work of your office(s) faithfully, to love the church and all its members, to live a life worthy of your calling and in submission to the government and discipline of the church? Each office bearer answers individually: By the grace of God, with all my heart, I do. Laying on of hands or raising the right hand in the gesture of blessing: May God, our heavenly Father, who has called you to your holy office, guide you by His Word, equip you with His Holy Spirit, and so bless your ministry that His church may increase, His kingdom be extended, and His name be praised. Amen. Office bearers to remain standing, facing the congregation who also stand: Congregation of our Lord Jesus Christ, to express your acceptance of these office bearers, you are asked to answer the following questions: 1. Do you, before God and one another, receive this servant / these servants as your minister/elder(s)/deacon(s)? Regarding ministers / elders: 2. Do you promise to receive the Word of truth from them in love and obedience as they seek to give you leadership and guidance in the work of the Lord? Regarding deacons: 3. Do you promise to enable the diaconate to function meaningfully in its ministry of compassion and mercy? 4. Do you promise to pray for these office bearers, respect and encourage them in their work, and faithfully work together with them to the honour and glory of Christ, the upbuilding of His church and the extension of His kingdom? Congregation, in response to these questions what is your answer? All members of the local church answer: By the grace of God, with all our heart, we do. All are seated. CHARGES 1. To the minister: I charge you, dear brother and fellow-servant in Christ: preach the Word; be prepared whether it is convenient for you or not; correct, rebuke and encourage — with great patience and careful instruction ...keep your head in all situations, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, discharge all duties of your ministry. Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved, a workman who does not need to be ashamed and who correctly handles the Word of truth. Not lording it over those entrusted to you, but setting an example for the believers and all men in speech, in life, in love, in faith and in purity. Do not be ashamed to testify about our Lord, but take your share of suffering for the gospel, by the power of God who has saved us and called us with a holy calling. And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the crown of glory that will never fade away. Pray continually for the church. To the congregation: And I charge you, people of God: welcome your minister in the Lord with great joy, and honour men like him. When you receive the Word of God through his preaching and teaching, then accept it not as the word of man but, as it actually is, the Word of God. Thus the peace of God shall be upon you, and believing in Christ, you will be saved — you and your households. Pray for him, accept him, support and encourage him in all that he does as a servant of the Lord. 2. To the elders: I charge you, dear brothers and fellow-servants in Christ: keep watch over yourselves and all the flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, not because you must but because you are willing, as God wants you to be, eager to serve; not lording it over those entrusted to you but being examples to them. Be diligent in these matters, watch your life and doctrine closely. Persevere in them, because if you do, you will save both yourself and your hearers. Pray continually for the church. To the congregation: And I charge you, people of God: respect those who work hard among you, who are over you in the Lord and admonish you. Hold them in the highest regard in love because of their work. Live in peace with each other. Obey your leaders and submit to their authority. They keep watch over you as men who must give account. Obey them so that their work will be a joy, not a burden, for that would be of no advantage to you. Sustain them in prayer, accept and encourage them as servants of the Lord. 3. To the deacons: I charge you, dear fellow-servants in Christ: Do your work with the same compassion as the Lord showed to those in need. When showing mercy, do it cheerfully.Help the needy and the afflicted, and have pity on the weak.Comfort them, both locally and elsewhere, with material support and the Word of God, with prayer and good advice. Encourage God's people to carry each other's burdens and in this way fulfil the law of Christ. Pray continually for the church. To the congregation: And I charge you, people of God: acknowledge the deacons as ministers of God's mercy and provide the diaconate with generous contributions. Excel in this grace of giving, showing thereby the sincerity of your love. For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich. Sustain them in prayer, accept and encourage them as servants of the Lord. It may be appropriate to have the newly ordained / installed office bearer(s) sign the Form of Subscription in the service. This Form should then first be read out for the information of the congregation, and may be found on page 185. Prayer: Our merciful Father in heaven, we thank You for providing faithful and gifted servants to minister to and build up the body of Christ. As these brothers assume the responsibilities of their office, we pray that You will fill them with the Holy Spirit. We ask that You will equip them with wisdom and give them strength for their task. May they be faithful workers in Your vineyard. Under their guidance let Your church grow in every spiritual grace, in faith which is open and unashamed, and in the committed service that promotes Your reign in the world. Deliver them from an attitude towards their office that is commonplace or self-assured. In their work grant them a humble dependence on Your grace, that they may come to You with all their needs. Help us, Your people, to accept them gladly, encourage them always, and respect them for the sake of Your precious Son, our Lord and King, in whose name we pray. Amen. documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/05 - Ordination and Installation of Office Bearers/02 - Form for the Ordination and Installation of Ministers.md
documents.text: Form For The Ordination / Installation Of Ministers THE OPENING OF THE SERVICE M "Comfort, comfort My people, says your God. speak tenderly to Jerusalem and proclaim to her that her hard service has been completed, that her sin has been paid for, C that she has received from the LORD's hand double for all her sins." M "A voice says, 'Cry out.' And I said, 'what shall I cry?' C 'All men are like grass, and all their glory is like the flowers of the field... The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the Word of our God stands for ever.' M You who bring good tidings to Zion, go up on a high mountain. C You who bring good tidings to Jerusalem, lift up your voice with a shout! M Lift it up, do not be afraid; say to the towns of Judah, 'Here is your God!'" C "He tends His flock like a shepherd: He gathers the lambs in His arms and carries them close to His heart!" M "You are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people belonging to God, C that we may declare the praises of Him who called us out of darkness into His wonderful light!" M Our help is in the name of the LORD C who made heaven and earth! M Who faithfully keeps His word C and never forsakes the works of His hands! M Grace unto you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ in the fellowship of the Holy Spirit. C Amen! The congregation sings (Psalm 100 or Psalm 113). CONFESSION AND ASSURANCE M The word of the LORD came to me: "Son of man, speak to your countrymen and say to them: 'When I bring the sword against a land, and the people of the land choose one of their men and make him their watchman, and he sees the sword coming against the land and blows the trumpet to warn the people, then if anyone hears the trumpet but does not take warning and the sword comes and takes his life, his blood will be on his own head. Since he heard the sound of the trumpet but did not take warning, his blood will be on his own head. If he had taken warning, he would have saved himself. But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the trumpet to warn the people and the sword comes and takes the life of one of them, that man will be taken away because of his sin, but I will hold the watchman accountable for his blood.' Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; so hear the word I speak and give them warning from Me. When I say to the wicked, 'O wicked man, you will surely die', and you do not speak to dissuade him from his ways, that wicked man will die for his sin, and I will hold you accountable for his blood. But if you do warn the wicked man to turn from his ways and he does not do so, he will die for his sin, but you will have saved yourself. Son of man, say to the house of Israel, 'This is what you are saying: C "Our offenses and sins weigh us down, and we are wasting away because of them. How then can we live?"' M Say to them, 'As surely as I live, declares the sovereign LORD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that they turn from their ways and live. Turn! Turn from your evil ways! Why will you die, O house of Israel?'" The congregation sings (Psalm 130 or selected verses from Psalm 51): M "Christ is the end of the law so that there may be righteousness for everyone who believes. Moses describes in this way the righteousness that is by the law: 'The man who does these things will live by them.' But the righteousness that is by faith says: 'Do not say in your heart, Who will ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down) or Who will descend into the deep?' (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead). But what does it say? 'The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart,' that is the word of faith we are proclaiming: that if you confess with your mouth, 'Jesus is Lord', and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved. C For it is with our heart that we believe and are justified, and it is with our mouth that we confess and are saved. M As the Scripture says, "Anyone who trusts in Him will never be put to shame." C For there is no difference between Jew and Gentile — the same Lord is Lord of all and richly blesses all who call on Him, for "everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved." M How then, can they call on the one they have not believed in? And how can they believe in the one of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone preaching to them? And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: C "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!" M Faith comes from hearing the message and the message is heard through the word of Christ." A psalm or hymn is sung expressing the joy of the gospel. M "Jesus said to Simon Peter, 'Simon, son of John, do you truly love Me more than these?' He said, Minister to be ordained / installed: 'Yes Lord, You know that I love You.' M Jesus said, 'Feed My lambs'. Again Jesus said, 'Simon, son of John, do you truly love Me?' And he answered, Minister to be ordained / installed: 'Yes, Lord, you know that I love You.' M Jesus said, 'Take care of My sheep.' M The third time He said... 'Simon, son of John, do you love Me?'... He said, Minister to be ordained / installed: 'Lord, You know all things, You know that I love You.' M 'Feed My sheep...Follow Me'." A psalm or hymn is to be sung, expressing love for the Lord. Then follows a prayer for which the following words may be used or in which the minister, using his own words, expresses the following thoughts: Almighty God and loving Father in our Lord Jesus Christ, We offer unto You thanksgiving and praise for having made known to us the gospel of Jesus Your Son. When we were dead in transgressions and sins He died our death and took away for ever the burden of Your holy anger. When He had finished bearing our punishment and paying the price for our redemption You raised Him up to a life that all who believe in Him will share for ever. We praise You for the Word made flesh and for the Scriptures which tell us about Him, shining as a light before our feet until the great morning will dawn when our faith shall be sight and our pilgrimage will be over. We bless You and thank You for the Holy Spirit guiding Your people in all Your truth. We thank You also, that, whereas Your whole Church is called to be the bearer of this good news in the world, You have given to her pastors and teachers to equip the saints for this ministry, to open Your Word to us and show us Your way of repentance, faith and joyful obedience. We pray that You will guide Your servants with Your holy Spirit, that they will humbly submit to the truth You have revealed, making their own thoughts captive to the obedience of Your Word. Encourage them with Your promises and make them bold with Your authority. Clothe them with holiness of life and give them compassion that they may reach out to those wandering as sheep without a shepherd. Here special points for intercession may be made, including the family of the ordinand. Now open our hearts to Your Word that we may receive it in humility and joy and be doers of that Word in our daily lives. For Jesus' sake, C Amen. THE MINISTRY OF THE WORD Scripture reading(s). Text and sermon. A psalm or hymn is sung. THE ORDINATION / INSTALLATION M Congregation of Jesus Christ: Your Session has previously made known to you the name of our brother Full Name called to the ministry of the Word and sacraments in this church. No one has brought forward anything lawful against his person or teaching. We shall therefore proceed, in the name of the Lord, to his ordination/installation. Let us first call to mind what God's Word teaches concerning this office within the church. All members of the Body of Christ are office-bearers, called to be prophets, priests and kings unto God, needing no mediators between God and man apart from Jesus Christ. Christ, however, gathering His church on earth, gave her as His gifts special office bearers, pastors and teachers, to prepare God's people for works of service. Servants they are of God and of His people, following in the footsteps of Him who came not to be served but to serve, giving His life as a Ransom for many. Servants they are of their risen Lord who said, "Whoever accepts anyone I send, accepts Me; and whoever accepts Me, accepts the One who sent Me." The first and foremost call of the minister of the Word is to preach the gospel of the kingdom, calling sinners to be reconciled to God, and nurturing believers in the faith and life of His kingdom. Humble and diligent daily study of God's Word will enable the servant of the gospel to proclaim and apply it in the public worship of the church, in the teaching of its youth, in the homes of its members and in confrontation with those outside. Feeding eagerly upon the Word he can feed others, refute errors, warn the wayward, comfort the grieving, and lead God's people into a joyful life of hope and obedience. C "Do good to Your servants and we will live; we will obey Your Word. Open our eyes that we may see wonderful things in Your law." M The minister of the Word is also called to administer the sacraments which Christ has given as signs and seals of His grace. Christ said, "Make disciples of all nations, baptising them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit" and, speaking of the Lord's Supper, "Do this in remembrance of Me." C "Christ is the Mediator of a new covenant that we who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance." M The minister of the Word is also called to give leadership in the service of prayer. Following his Master and the apostles, he will bring the needs of God's people before the throne of grace and ensure that, in public worship, "requests, prayers, intercession and thanksgiving be made for everyone — for kings and all those in authority," for the needs of God's people and for those in the world around them. C "May our prayer be set before You like incense; may the lifting up of our hands be like the evening sacrifice." M Together with the elders, the minister of the Word is called to shepherd the people of God in the Christian life, giving guidance and counsel, keeping the church of God in good order and discipline. Both in encouragement and rebuke they are to make faithful use of the keys of the kingdom, binding on earth what shall be bound in heaven, and loosing on earth what shall be loosed in heaven. C "The LORD is God! It is He who made us, and we are His. We are His people, the sheep of His pasture." M And now, brother Name , in order that it may be clear to us all that you are ready to accept this office, will you please stand and answer the following questions before God and His people. The ordinand stands. 1. Do you believe in your heart that, in the call of this congregation it is the Lord Jesus Christ Himself who called you to be His servant, minister of His gospel? 2. Do you believe the Scriptures of the Old and New Testament to be the Word of God, the only infallible rule of faith and practice, and do you accept the doctrinal standards of the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia as being in harmony with these Scriptures? Do you promise to proclaim and defend this gospel, and to reject all teachings that contradict it; to speak against all injustice and all untruth, and model for this congregation God's concern for compassion, justice and peace? 3. Do you promise to carry out the duties of your office faithfully, to love the church and all its members, and to live a life that is worthy of your calling? 4. Do you promise to submit to the government and discipline of the church, when it calls you to the obedience of the Word of God? The ordinand answers: By the grace of God, with all my heart, I do. If this is an ordination, the ordinand shall now kneel. All ministers present and such elders as are appointed to do so by Session, shall lay their right hand on his head. If this is an installation of a minister already ordained before, the installing minister shall lift his hand in the gesture of blessing. M God our heavenly Father, who has called you to this holy office, enlighten you with His Spirit, strengthen you with His hand, and so govern and use you in your ministry, that it shall bear rich fruit both for this life and for the life to come, to the glory of His name and the coming of the kingdom of His Son Jesus Christ. C Amen. The newly ordained minister shall remain standing and face the congregation. The officiating minister shall ask the congregation to arise and will address them: M People of God, members of this congregation, do you receive this servant of your Lord and Redeemer from His hand, do you promise to receive the Word of truth from his lips in love and obedience, to remember him in prayer and encourage him in his work? Do you promise to work together with him and the other office bearers in making known the gospel of Christ? C By the grace God, with all our heart, we do. Here a psalm (suggested: Psalm 134) or hymn shall be sung. Then all shall be seated. The officiating minister or another appointed by Session shall present the charges: CHARGES M Dear brother and fellow-servant in Christ. Keep watch over yourself and all the flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you a guardian. Be a shepherd of the church of your Lord, which He bought with His own blood. Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved, a workman who does not need to be ashamed and who correctly handles the Word of truth. Do not be domineering over those entrusted to you, but rather, to the believers and to all people, be an example in speech and life, in love, in faith and in purity. Do not be ashamed of testifying about our Lord but by the power of God who saved us and called us to a holy life, take your share of suffering for the sake of the gospel. Then, when the Chief Shepherd appears, you too will receive the crown of glory that will never fade away. And you, congregation of our Lord Jesus, receive your minister in the Lord with all joy and hold him in honour. When he preaches to you from the Holy Scriptures, accept it not as the word of man, but as it actually is, the Word of God. Then the peace of God shall enter your lives and your homes, and believing in Christ, you shall inherit eternal life. No man can do these things in his own strength. Let us therefore call upon the name of God: Merciful Father, we thank You that Your Son, our Lord Jesus, through the service of men, gathers His Church from a lost human race unto life eternal. We thank You for this servant of Yours, sent to Your people as a messenger of Your peace. Fill him mightily with Your Holy Spirit. Enlighten his mind to know the truth of Your Word. Give him the words so that he may fearlessly make known the mystery of the gospel. Endow him with wisdom to give care and guidance to the people among whom You have placed him. Through his ministry, preserve Your church in peace, and make her grow in love, hope and joyful witness to those around her. Give Your servant courage to face hardships, and compassion in the face of sorrow, both in others and in himself. Make him always willing to repent of evil and — with courage — to fight the devil both in his own life and in the lives of those entrusted to him. Give him the joy of Your salvation, to be his strength until he, with all those who love Christ's appearance, shall see Him face to face. This we ask in the name of the Lord Jesus, who taught us to say: C Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name, Your kingdom come, Your will be done on earth as in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. Forgive us our sins, as we forgive those who sin against us. Lead us not into temptation but deliver us from the evil one. For the kingdom, the power, and the glory are yours now and for ever. Amen. It may be appropriate to have the newly ordained / installed minister sign the Form of Subscription in the service. This Form should then first be read out for the information of the congregation, and may be found on page 185. The offering is taken, a psalm or hymn is sung and the service ends with the benediction. It is assumed that the service is led by a minister (or ministers) other than the one who is to be ordained/installed, except for the final benediction which, traditionally, is often given by the new minister. Furthermore, there may be circumstances in which the preaching of the inaugural sermon by the newly ordained/installed minister is to take place in the same service in which he is ordained/installed. The point at which this is to take place would be after the "charges". Even if both ministers keep their sermon short, it makes for a long service, however. It is suggested that the two men involved cooperate in such a way that the two sermons, as much as possible, form a unity.This form is to be used flexibly. As with other participatory forms, one of the main aims is to spread the teaching element so that it can be more easily followed and absorbed by the congregation. Rather than using this form for a whole service, Sessions may also begin using it from page 285, "The Ordination/Installation." M = Minister. C = Congregation, in unison. Isaiah 40:1-2. Isaiah 40:6, 8-9 Isaiah 40:11 1 Peter 2:9 Ezekiel 33:1-11 Romans 10:4-15 Romans 10:17 John 21:15-19 Ordination if this is a first charge, installation if it is a subsequent one. documents.title: Form for the Ordination and Installation of Elders and Deacons
documents.groupTitle: Ordination and Installation of Office Bearers
documents.path: The Liturgical Forms/05 - Ordination and Installation of Office Bearers/03 - Form for the Ordination and Installation of Elders and Deacons.md
documents.text: Form For The Ordination / Installation Of Elders And Deacons THE OPENING OF THE SERVICE M Praise, O servants of the LORD, praise the name of the LORD! C Let the name of the LORD be praised, both now and for evermore. M From the rising of the sun to the place where it sets, C the name of the LORD is to be praised! M The LORD is exalted over all the nations, C His glory above the heavens. M Who is like the LORD our God, the One who sits enthroned on high, who stoops down to look on the heavens and the earth? He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap; C Praise the LORD! Hallelujah! M Our help is in the name of the LORD C Who made heaven and earth! M Who faithfully keeps His Word C and never forsakes the works of His hands! M Grace unto you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ in the fellowship of the Holy Spirit. C Amen! The congregation sings (Psalm 84, 122, or another suitable psalm or hymn). CONFESSION AND ASSURANCE M "This is the message we have heard from Him and declare to you: God is light; in Him there is no darkness at all. C If we claim to have fellowship with Him yet walk in the darkness, we lie and do not live by the truth. M But if we walk in the light, as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus, His Son, purifies us from all sin. If we claim to be without sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us. C If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness." The congregation sings a psalm or hymn expressing confession of sin. M "Dear friends, let us love one another, for love comes from God... This is how God showed His love among us: He sent His one and only Son into the world that we might live through Him. C This is love, not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as an atoning sacrifice for our sins." M "For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith — and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God — not by works, so that no one can boast. C For we are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus, to do good works which God prepared in advance for us to do." The congregation sings a psalm or hymn expressing the joy of the gospel. M "God, who said, 'Let light shine out of darkness,' made His light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Christ. C But we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this all-surpassing power is from God and not from us. M We are hard pressed on every side, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair; persecuted, but not abandoned; struck down, but not destroyed. C We always carry around in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body." M "Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; the old has gone, the new has come! C All this is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation." M "Therefore I urge you, brothers, in view of God's mercy, offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God — this is your spiritual act of worship. Do not conform any longer to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God's will is — His good, pleasing and perfect will... Do not think of yourselves more highly than you ought, but rather, think of yourselves with sober judgment, in accordance with the measure of faith God has given you... C In Christ, we who are many form one body, and each member belongs to all the others. We have different gifts, according to the grace given us. M If a man's gift is prophesying, let him use it in proportion to his faith. If it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach; C if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is contributing to the needs of others, let him give generously. M If it is leadership, let him govern diligently; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully." The congregation sings a psalm or hymn expressing joy in serving God, one another, and a world in need. Then follows a prayer for which the following words may be used or in which the minister, using his own words, expresses the following thoughts: Almighty God and loving Father in our Lord Jesus Christ, how can we ever thank You enough for the joyful sound of the gospel in which You assure us that in Christ Jesus all our sins are forgiven and our life is renewed. We thank You for freely giving this marvellous gift of new life to us as Your church. We thank You that we share as Your people this costly treasure and may share it in turn with the needy world around us. We thank You that in this congregation, too, Your love has made and is making us into one body with many members, and that You are giving us people endowed with Your gifts to help equip us for our witness to the gospel. We thank You for the brothers who served among us, and we thank You for the families who supported them. Lord, we need You for all we need in this church. What can we give others that You do not give us first? In all our doing and giving we fall so short of Your generosity! But we thank You that You do not leave us on our own: Your Son promised to be with us even to the end of the age — Your Spirit guides us into all truth. Now You have given us these servants to serve as Your instruments, and we pray that Your Spirit will shape them for their work. Enable them to help us be bearers of Your good news in this day and in this place. Here special points of intercession can be included. Now open our hearts to Your Word that we may receive it in humility and joy and be doers of that Word in our daily lives. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. C Amen. THE MINISTRY OF THE WORD Scripture reading(s). Text and sermon. A psalm or hymn is sung. THE ORDINATION / INSTALLATION M Congregation of Jesus Christ: Your Session has previously made known to you Names called to the office of elder and the name(s) of ____Names___ called to the office of deacon in this church. No one has brought forward anything lawful against their person or teaching. We shall therefore proceed, in the name of the Lord, to their ordination [and] installation. Let us first call to mind what God's Word teaches concerning these offices within the church. All members of the Body of Christ are office bearers, called to be prophets,1 priests and kings unto God, needing no mediators between God and man apart from Jesus Christ. Christ, however, gathering His church on earth, gave her as His gifts special office bearers to equip and prepare God's people for the work of service. Servants they are of God and of His people, following in the footsteps of Him who came not to be served but to serve, giving His life as a Ransom for many. Servants they are of their risen Lord who said, "Whoever accepts anyone I send, accepts Me; and whoever accepts Me, accepts the One who sent Me." C "We are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people belonging to God, that we may declare the praises of Him who called us out of darkness into His wonderful light!" When elders are ordained / installed: M Elders serve by governing the church in Christ's name. They received this task when Christ entrusted the apostles and their successors with the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Thus elders are responsible for the spiritual well-being of God's people. They are to provide for true preaching and teaching, regular celebration of the sacraments, and faithful counsel and discipline. Their call is also to promote fellowship among believers, hospitality and witness to all people, and good order in the church. C "For the grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all men. It teaches us to say 'no' to ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright and godly lives in this present age, while we wait for the blessed hope — the glorious appearing of our great God and Saviour, Jesus Christ, who gave Himself for us to redeem us from all wickedness and to purify for Himself a people that are His very own, eager to do what is good. These then are the things you should teach. Encourage and rebuke with all authority. Do not let anyone despise you." When deacons are ordained / installed: M Deacons serve by showing mercy to the church and to all people. They received this task in the early church when the apostles designated special persons for the work of mercy. The deacons stimulate relief in Christ's name for victims of poverty, distress and injustice. Thereby they show that Christians live by the Spirit of the kingdom, fervently desiring to give life the shape of things to come. In the household of God, deacons are therefore called to assess needs, promote stewardship, and develop programs of assistance. When carried out with words of Christian encouragement, their work is done as unto the Lord Himself. C "Then the King will say... 'Come, you who are blessed by my Father; take your inheritance, the kingdom prepared for you since the creation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave Me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me something to drink, I was a stranger and you invited Me in, I needed clothes and you clothed Me, I was sick and you looked after Me, I was in prison and you came to visit Me... For whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me.'" M These tasks of elders and deacons call for believers who are mature in the faith, whose lives are Christ-like, and who exercise their offices with diligent study of the Scriptures, with prayer, patience and humility. VOWS M Brothers Names , to express your acceptance of the office of Elder / Deacon, you are asked to stand, and here in the presence of God and His church to answer the following questions: 1. Do you believe that, in the call of this congregation, you are being called by God Himself to serve in this holy office / these holy offices? 2. Do you believe that the Scriptures of the Old and New Testament are the Word of God and that in them the way of salvation is taught completely, and do you accept the confessional standards of the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia as being in harmony with these Scriptures? Do you promise to defend this gospel and to reject all teachings that contradict it; to speak against all injustice and all untruth, and model for this congregation God's concern for compassion, justice and peace? 3. Do you promise to carry out the work of your offices faithfully, to love the church and all its members, to live a life worthy of your calling and in submission to the government and discipline of the church? Each office bearer answers individually: By the grace of God, with all my heart, I do Laying on of hands or raising the right hand in the gesture of blessing: M May God, our heavenly Father, who has called you to your holy office, guide you by His Word, equip you with His Holy Spirit, and so bless your ministry that His church may increase, His kingdom be extended, and His name be praised. C Amen. Office bearer(s) remain standing, facing the congregation who also stand. M Congregation of our Lord Jesus Christ, to express your acceptance of this/these office bearers, you are asked to answer these questions: 1. Do you, before God and one another, receive this servant / these servants as your elder(s) [and] deacon(s)? Regarding elders: 2. Do you promise to receive the Word of truth from them in love and obedience as they seek to give you leadership and guidance in the work of the Lord? Regarding deacons: 3. Do you promise to enable the diaconate to function meaningfully in its ministry of compassion and mercy? 4. Do you promise to pray for these office bearers, respect and encourage them in their work, and faithfully work together with them to the honour and glory of Christ, the upbuilding of His church and the extension of His kingdom? Congregation, in response to all these questions what is your answer? All members of the local church answer: C By the grace of God, with all our heart, we do. The congregation sings Psalm 134, and is then seated. CHARGES To Elders: M I charge you, elders, to "take heed of yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you guardians, to feed the church of God which He obtained with the blood of His own Son." Be a warm friend and Christ-like example to children. Give clear, cheerful and unpretentious guidance to the young people, who often wrestle with the overpowering spirits of this age. By word and example bear up God's people in their pain and weakness and celebrate their joys with them. Attentively and regularly encourage the aged with the hope of biblical promises. Be (a) wise counsellor(s) who support and strengthen the ministers of the Word. Be compassionate, yet firm, and consistent in rebuke and discipline. Master the Scriptures which alone can make God's people wise unto salvation. Pray continually for the church. Remember at all times that, if you would truly be spiritual leaders in the household of faith, your entire lives must be mastered by your Lord. To Deacons: I charge you, deacons, to inspire faithful stewardship in this congregation. Remind us that "From everyone who has been given much, much will be demanded; and from the one who has been entrusted with much, much more will be asked." Weigh up the needs of causes and use the resources of this church with discernment. Prompt us to seize new opportunities to worship God with offerings of wealth, time and ability. Realise that benevolence is a quality of our life in Christ, and not merely a matter of financial assistance. Therefore, be ministers of mercy to rich and poor alike, both within and outside the church. Teach us to be merciful. Be discreetly compassionate to the needy. Encourage them with words that create hope in their hearts and with deeds that bring joy into their lives. Guide them to resources beyond your own. Study the structures and patterns of modern society, so that you may be counsellors to their victims and prophetic critics of waste, injustice, and selfishness. Let your lives be above reproach, lived as an example of Christ Jesus whose mind is being shaped within you. To the Congregation, in all cases: I charge you, people of God, to receive your office bearers as Christ's gift to the church. Recognise in all of them your Lord's provision for healthy congregational life. Hold them in honour; take their counsel seriously; accept their help with thanks. Sustain them in prayer and encourage them with your support, especially when they feel the burdens of responsibility. Acknowledge them as the Lord's servants among you, and submit to them as you do to Christ. Let us pray. Our merciful Father in heaven, we thank You that You have provided faithful and gifted people to serve as elders and deacons. As these new office bearers assume their responsibilities, fill them with Your Spirit, endow them with Your wisdom, and grant them strength from on high. May they be faithful workers in Your vineyard. Under their guidance may Your church grow in every spiritual grace, in faith which is open and unashamed, and in the committed service that promotes Your reign in the world. Deliver them from an attitude towards office that is commonplace or self-assured. In their work, grant them a sense of sustained awe which is rooted in daily adoration of You, their Lord. Through them may Your name be honoured and Your church be served. Grant us, Your people, to accept them gladly, encourage them always and respect them for the sake of Your precious Son, our Lord, in whose name we pray. C Amen. It may be appropriate to have the newly ordained/installed office bearer(s) sign the Form of Subscription in the service. This Form should then first be read out for the information of the congregation, and may be found on page 185. Rather than using this form for a whole service, Sessions could also begin using it from page 295, "The Ordination / Installation". M = Minister. C = Congregation, in unison.
