documents.text: Rules for the Final Examination of Candidates for the Ministry of the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia Appendix: Examination Rules — Adopted at Synod 2024 General The purpose of this examination shall be to ascertain whether the candidate is able to pursue the work of the ministry of the Word and sacraments in the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia to the edification of the people of God and the progress of the church. Classis needs to ensure that it can heartily recommend the candidate for ordination. The Classis shall not conduct this examination in such a way that it is a mere repetition of the college examination. This examination is not an open book exam and is not supposed to be of an academic but ecclesiastical nature. The churches must know whether the candidate is sound in doctrine and is able to apply his knowledge in a suitable manner. A. Requirements 1. A statement from the Reformed Theological College (RTC) – or equivalent institution indicating that the Candidate has successfully completed the regular, prescribed study in theology, and testifying to his Christian conduct while a student. 2. A statement from the Session (or Church Council) to which the Candidate belonged during his candidature or training, regarding his doctrine and conduct. 3. A statement from a medical doctor about the Candidate’s physical fitness. 4. A statement from classical deputies who have discussed with the Candidate the motives causing him to seek the ministry. B. Examination guidelines for Specimen Sermon 1. The final exam is to be held in the Classis, where the candidate is completing his vicariate or training. 2. The Classis will ensure that two Synodical Deputies from two separate Classis outside the examining Classis be present. These deputies will have a voice and a vote, but not the right of veto. 3. The exam will follow the following process: - a. The Candidate will be asked to provide a specimen sermon with exegetical notes on a passage prescribed to him by the appointed sermon examiners. The candidate shall forward copies of the specimen sermon to the Classis Clerk at least one month prior to the examination for distribution to the examiners and to the sessions. This sermon will be examined and must meet the standard required to be sustained. - b. The Candidate will also provide two further sermons with exegetical notes, of his own choice, and these sermons must also meet the standard to sustain an exam. Each of these two sermons should address a different genre of Scripture; either Old Testament History, Wisdom, Prophecy or Psalms; or New Testament Gospel, Parable, Epistles or Revelation. - c. The classical examiners shall evaluate the content of these sermons on the basis of the guidelines adopted by Synod 1985 Art 82.2: - i. Accuracy of exegesis. - ii. Does the outline carry the text? - iii. Is the context, including the historical redemptive, taken into account? - iv. Is the basic thrust Christ-centred? - v. Is the sermon doctrinally sound? - vi. Is the teaching applied in a manner consistent with the text? - vii. Is the theme developed in a coherent logical manner? - d. The classis examiners shall give reasons at the examination why the Classis should either sustain or not sustain the sermon. Classis shall decide on the recommendations of the examiners before the candidate preaches the sermon. - e. Where the Classis decides to sustain the sermon, the examination continues and the candidate shall preach the sermon. The Classis shall judge if the candidate shows gifts of communication and the deliver is edifying, taking into account the experience of the candidate. - f. A two-thirds majority is required to sustain the sermon part of the exam. - g. In the event that the Classis decides for serious reasons not to sustain the sermon, the candidate shall not be asked to preach the sermon but continue with the oral section of the examination. If the Classis sustains the oral examination, then the candidate shall, before the next meeting of the Classis, prepare another sermon on a text chosen by himself and forward copies of this sermon and brief exegetical notes to the Classis Clerk, who will distribute it to the examiners and to all the Sessions at least one month prior to the next Classis meeting. Classis at this meeting shall hear the evaluation of the examiners and decide whether or not to sustain the sermon. If sustained, the Classis proceeds with 3e with the exception, of course, of the remainder of the examination. C. Examination guidelines for Oral examination 1. Exegesis: The examination in the exegesis of both Old and New Testaments shall cover one or two passages from one chapter in each Testament. The assignment of the two chapters shall be made at least three weeks prior to the examination. The reading of the Bible in the original languages and a lengthy discussion of introductory problems shall be omitted. The Classis shall satisfy itself that the candidate is able to expound the Scriptures. The candidate shall be examined in each Testament for 15 minutes. 2. Dogmatics: The manner in which a candidate is to be examined must be of a practical rather than of an academic nature. The purpose is not to repeat the final college examination. The churches may leave this to the RTC or equivalent institution. The churches have to assure themselves that the candidate is sound in doctrine and is capable of giving a clear exposition of the Reformed doctrines and of defending the Reformed position over against heresies which are popular in our time, in order that as shepherd of Christ’s flock he may be able to protect that flock and “hold firmly to the trustworthy message as it has been taught, so that he can encourage others by sound doctrine and refute those who oppose it” (Tit 1:9). The candidate shall be examined for at least 30 minutes in this subject. 3. The oral sections for the examination include the following: - i. Old Testament & New Testament Exegesis (15 Minutes each), - ii. Dogmatics, Ethics & Symbolics (45 Minutes), - iii. Church History (15 Minutes), - iv. Church polity (10 Minutes) - v. Knowledge of Scripture (10 Minutes) D. After the Examination 1. On completion of the sermon and oral sections of the examination, Classis requires a two-third majority or more to sustain the exam. 2. After the successful completion of the examination, the Candidate shall subscribe to the Confessional Standards of the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia in the presence of the Classis. 3. The Classis shall give the Candidate a statement which allows him to be ordained as a minister of Word and sacraments. 4. After the successful completion of the examination, the Candidate may receive calls immediately but cannot accept a call to serve a calling church until six weeks have expired (As per Synod Decision 1965 Art 30.1).

documents.text: The Acts of Synod 2024 Section I — The Acts of Synod 2024 of the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia · Oasis Church, Queensland, Australia · 19–23 May 2024 Article 1: Opening On behalf of the calling church – Oasis Church - Rev Adam Schoenmaker called the 27th Synod of the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia to order and led the Synod in a meditation on Revelation 2:1-7, prayer and praise. Article 2: Credentials It was noted that the following brethren were seated as Primary Delegates: 1. From Classis New South Wales: Minister: Rev Dan Kroon Minister: Rev Lourens Nel Elder: Br Tony Deenick Elder: Br Frank Jobse (Rev Alan Douma and Rev Ben Peletier were noted as being Alternate delegates.) 2. From Classis Queensland: Minister: Rev Josh Hartog Minister: Rev Craig van Echten Elder: Br Marty Robinson Elder: Br Jason Ring (Rev Andrew de Vries and Br John Van Dijk were noted as being Alternate delegates.) 3. From Classis Tasmania: Minister: Rev Isaac Lee Minister: Rev Nathanael Remminga Elder: Br Peter Vander Schoor Elder: Rev Pieter Tuit (Rev Jack Kapinga was noted as being Alternate delegate.) 4. From Classis Gippsland: Minister: Rev Glenn Dekker Minister: Rev Stephen Coleman Elder: Br Corey Van Garderen Elder: Rev John Zuidema (Rev Richard Schoenmaker and Br Herman Westendorp were noted as being alternate delegates.) 5. From Classis Maroondah: Minister: Rev Isaac Overton Minister: Rev Chris Pretorius Elder: Rev Lucas Edwards Elder: Br Peter William (Rev Tim Gray, Rev Andy Buchan and Br Chris Bongers were noted as being alternate delegates.) 6. From Classis Western Australia: Minister: Rev Andrew Nugteren Minister: Rev Ben Murphy Elder: Br Brendan Meyerink Elder: Br Frank van den Bos (Rev Joe Vermeulen and Br Alex Thompson were noted as being alternate delegates.) Article 3: Election and Confirmation of Moderamen Synod acknowledged and confirmed the results of the election of the Moderamen by the delegates via email during January 2024, involving the Synodical Administrator and two scrutineers from the calling church (Oasis Church). The following brethren have been duly elected: - Chairman: Rev. John Zuidema - Vice-Chairman: Rev. Andrew Nugteren - First Clerk: Elder Tony Deenick (Minute Clerk), - Second Clerk: Rev Pieter Tuit (Correspondence Clerk). Article 4: Constitution of Synod The members of the Moderamen were invited to take their place and the Chairman, Rev John Zuidema addressed the Synod briefly. He welcomed everyone to Synod 2024 and thanked the convening Oasis Church and the organizers for the preparations of Synod 2024. John then stated on behalf of the Moderamen that they felt honoured to be serving the Lord and the church in this way and pledged to do their utmost to serve the Synod well. John also requested help by keeping the debate/speeches focused. If points have already been discussed, delegates don’t need to repeat it. He urged delegates to represent their Churches and Classes well and to model patience, kindness and all the Spirit’s fruit as they participated in the work of Synod. John advised that Alternate Delegates are welcome to take the seat of those delegates moving to the Moderamen table but are to be aware that they are not taking the place of Primary Delegates and therefore do not have voting rights. John noted that in other cases where an Alternate Delegate replaces a Primary Delegate (e.g. when leaving the meeting) they should advise the Moderamen at the time of the change. Delegates moving amendments were asked to email them to Phil Schouten. Alternate delegates taking the place of those on the Moderamen were: - Classis NSW: Alan Douma. - Classis Tasmania: Rev Jack Kapinga. - Classis Gippsland: Herman Westendorp. (Synod took note of the passing into glory of Rev. Fred Vander Bom during the past inter-synodical period and Pieter Tuit gave thanks for his work in the denomination and prayed for his wife Helen.) Article 5: Advisers The Moderamen proposed and Synod accepted that: 1. Rev. Drs Phillip Scheepers and Stephen Lewis, be seated as Advisers, as per Church Order Art 48.c. 2. Rev Clinton Berends, our Ministry Development Coordinator (MDC), be seated as an Advisor, as per Church Order Art 48.d. Article 6: Agreement with Confessional Standards All primary delegates, and alternate delegates present, as well as Synod’s advisers, signified their agreement with the Confessional Standards of our Church by rising. Article 7: Matters of Procedure Synod decided on the following matters of procedure: 1. That, concerning the right of floor, the order will be similar to the previous Synod, and will be determined by the Chairman as appropriate. However, in general (and in keeping with the Rules for Procedure & Debate, adopted by Synod 1982, Art 29), delegates to the Synod shall have precedence over all other speakers, apart from a reporter for a committee who is not a delegate, and priority shall be given to those who have not already spoken. Advisors, fraternal delegates, and any office bearer of the CRCA who requests to be heard may be granted the floor by the Chairman as time and circumstances permit. No one shall speak longer than ten minutes, unless the synod, by a majority vote, permits him to extend his remarks. 2. To abide by the Rules of Debate, as found under “Appendix – Procedure & Debate” in the CRCA Decision Book. 3. To adopt the following time schedule: Morning session: 9.00 am – 10.40 am / 11.00 am – 12.30 pm Afternoon session: 2.00 pm – 3.40 pm / 4.00 pm – 5.30 pm Evening session: 7.30 pm – 9.00 pm 4. To adopt the following time limits: 1. that introduction of committee reports shall ordinarily be limited to five minutes; 2. that, as a general rule, any other speech be limited to ten minutes; 3. that addresses by Fraternal Delegates (and Observers, if applicable) be limited to ten minutes and our replies to five minutes. 5. That the reporters of all committees be required to organise recommendations contained in their Reports as follows: 1. recommendations which do not require Synod to make changes or to do anything new are to be grouped together and voted on ‘in block’; 2. recommendations which are likely to be passed unanimously by Synod are to be grouped together and voted on ‘in block’; 3. remaining recommendations are to be voted on separately. 6. Re devotions: 1. To set aside up to thirty minutes each morning for devotions, to be led by ministers from the Convening Church, RTC Faculty members and Rev Clinton Berends 2. That other devotions be taken as per the Devotion Roster circulated at the start of Synod. The brothers leading these devotions are reminded to keep track of specific prayer requests made during the session preceding their turn on the roster. 7. That the checking and approval of the Minutes of the previous day’s sessions be done after morning tea each day. 8. To appoint the following press reporter: 1. Rev Pieter Tuit for condensed news items (to be approved by the Moderamen) for uploading onto the CRCA Website. 9. Re the rate of reimbursement from synodical funds for travel on behalf of Synod and the denomination: 1. that reimbursement for car travel during the next inter-synodical period be set at 50 cents per kilometre. 2. that reimbursement for interstate travel during the next inter-synodical period be limited to the value of the discount air fare available at the time; 3. that reimbursement for travel to and from this Synod is payable at the above rates to primary delegates, advisers, and those coming to Synod to report on the work of its deputies when the committee is not otherwise represented, with the limitation of 9.2, above, for interstate travel. 10. Regarding meals at Synod’s expense: 1. that all meals be provided to all those who have registered to attend this Synod or part thereof. 2. that casual visitors be requested to pay for meals at a rate of $10 for lunch and $15 for dinner. 11. To note that only the decisions of Synod and not the full discussion will be minuted by the Minute Clerk. 12. To appoint the following ad hoc committee: 1. Financial Watchdog: - Troy Vander Noord plus - Herman Westendorp - Chris Bongers Article 8: Fraternal Delegate and Presenters Fraternal Delegates from within Australia and overseas were recognised, welcomed and granted leave to speak in the debates. 1. Fraternal Delegates present at various times during Synod: - Reformed Churches of New Zealand (RCNZ): Rev Reinier Noppers - Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC): John Terpstra - Presbyterian Church of Australia (PCA): Rev Lesleigh Hall - Presbyterian Church of Eastern Australia (PCEA): Rev Jim Klazinga - United Reformed Churches of North America (URCNA): Rev Stephen Wetmore - An apology was received from Rev. Stefaans de Bruyn and the Reformed Churches of South Africa (RCSA). 2. Presentations Synod gratefully received the following presentations during the course of the week: - Preliminary - A service of Prayer and Word was held in the Oasis Church, Bray Park, on Sunday 19th May 2024 at 6 pm, under the supervision of the Oasis Church. Members of the elected Moderamen of Synod 2024 led in worship. Rev John Zuidema brought God’s Word from Exodus 19 and Hebrews 12:18-29. - Fraternal Greetings: Reformed Churches of New Zealand (RCNZ): Rev. Reinier Noppers - CRCA Women’s Convention: Jack Kapinga addressed the meeting on the forthcoming CRCA Women’s Convention - International Justice Mission (IJM): Christian Koelbach addressed the Synod on the work of IJM - World Transform and IndiWay: Rev. Bert Kuipers - Reformed Theological College: Principal and Lecturer in Missions and Church History, Dr Phillip Scheepers - Fraternal Greetings: United Reformed Churches of North America (URCNA): Rev Stephen Wetmore - Fraternal Greetings: Presbyterian Church of Eastern Australia (PCEA): Rev Jim Klazinga - Bible League Address: Hilton Edwards addressed the Synod on the work of the Bible League - Reformed Theological College (RTC): Presentation from Dr Phillip Scheepers, Mr. Chris Bongers and Mr. Ken Dean reported on the work of the RTC. - Fraternal Greetings: Presbyterian Church of Australia (PCA): Rev Lesleigh Hall - SWIM: Br. Rod Peet gave a presentation on the work of SWIM. - Fraternal Greetings: Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC): John Terpstra - Ministry Development Coach: (MDC) Rev. Clinton Berends - Reformed Theological College: Lecturer in Old Testament and Hebrew, Dr Stephen Lewis Article 9: Correspondence Synod has received no correspondence for information and/or action. Article 10: Websites Consolidation [Overture 1 – Classis Maroondah] (Minutes Articles 10) Synod decided: 1. To instruct the Synodical Administrator to ensure that all CRCA synodical committees and employees have a common webhost to reduce costs to the denomination and simplify hosting requirements. 2. That all CRCA synodical committees and employee websites use standardised templates and menus to make denominational websites easier to navigate. Also ensuring that users can cross browse denominational, committee and employee websites with ease. Article 11: Updating Denominational Terms [Overture 2 - Classis Queensland] (Minutes Articles 11 and 40) The following motions were lost: 1. That vicariate be renamed minister apprenticeship, and vicar be renamed apprentice minister apprentice. 2. That Synod be renamed National Assembly, and that the Classis be renamed Regional Assembly. 3a. That Moderamen be renamed moderators as in national assembly moderators, or regional assembly moderators. The following motion was withdrawn: 3b. That the Interim Committee be renamed National Interim Committee, and Regional Interim Committee. Article 12: Overseas Mission Review Committee [Report 2, Convenor Dr Phillip Scheepers] (Minutes Article 12) Synod decided: 1. To receive this report. 2. That a ‘CRCA World Mission Committee’ be established as a subcommittee of GROW 3. That the composition and mandate of the committee be based on this report will include a brief quarterly report to the churches. 4. That Synod appoint the founding chairman of the committee. 5. That the committee will develop their specific mandate within 120 days of Synod. Once finalised, the mandate shall be approved by the majority of Classes. Article 13: Forms for Baptism Review [Report 3, Convenor Rev. KJ Tromp] (Minutes Article 13) Synod decided: 1. To receive this report. 2. To change the title of the baptismal forms for children to “The Baptism of the Children of Believers”. 3. To keep the Form 1 unchanged. 4. To make minor changes to the language of Form 2 as per Appendix 1. 5. The newly written form as per Appendix 1 be added as a new form (with the minor changes foreshadowed and accepted by the committee.) 6. To store and distribute all revised liturgical forms electronically. 7. That the newly written form be redesignated Form 1 and that the existing Form 1 be redesignated as Form 4. Article 14: Children and the Lord’s Supper - Overture [Overture 6 - CRC Toowoomba, CRC Tivoli & Christian Reformation Community Church, Inala] (Minutes Articles 14 & 39) The following motions were lost: 1. That a public profession of faith be required of all children prior to participation in the sacrament of Lord’s Supper. 2. That the qualifications for children coming to the Lord’s Supper table be amended as follows: - i. They must profess faith in Jesus and be baptised. - ii. There must be age-appropriate evidence of this faith being lived out. - iii. They must be able to articulate the content of the gospel as summarised in the Apostles Creed. - iv. They must be able to understand what it means to remember Christ’s death (v.25), proclaim Christ’s death (v.26), and to discern the body (v.29). - v. They must be capable of examining themselves without the assistance of an adult. - vi. They must understand that the bread represents Jesus’ body, and that the wine/juice represents His blood. They must understand that the supper is more than mere remembrance, but that they are spiritually nourished by Christ as they participate in faith at the table. - vii. They must be aware of, and understand, the dangers of participating unworthily in the supper. 3. That the Guidelines for Sessions who are assessing a child’s readiness to participate in the Lord’s Supper be adopted. 4. That we consult with the churches in Ecclesiastical Fellowship with the CRCA to ascertain the implications of our decisions on children at the Lord’s Supper made at Synod 2022 and Synod 2024. The following recommendation was withdrawn: 5. That a study committee be formed to consider the implications on how we work together as a denomination in view of our decisions on children at the Lord’s Supper. Synod “laid on the table” the following recommendation: 6. That each church has the freedom to supervise the table according to their own conscience and local practice. This means that if you are visiting or transferring to another CRCA church, you are required to submit to the local practice. [From Minutes Article 39: Children at the Lord’s Supper Ad Hoc Committee] Synod decided: 7. That each session/church council has the freedom to add additional qualifications (to those adopted by Synod 2022, Article 30, 4i-vi) when assessing the credibility of a child's faith for the purposes of determining if a child will be admitted to the Lord's Supper table. Those transferring into or visiting a church will have to submit to the local practice. Article 15: Children at the Lord’s Supper (Membership) Report [Report 1, Convenor – Rev Ben Murphy] (Minutes Article 15 & 48) Synod decided: 1. To receive this report. The following motion did not reach the required majority (2/3rds) for changes to the Church Order so was lost: 2. That the denomination moves to having only one category “Members.” All those who are baptised into the church, either as infants or later in life, be added to church membership and be considered full members. As a result, the following recommendations lapsed: 3. That churches, for their own record keeping and pastoral care, would have a list of those members who profess faith in Christ and participate in Lord’s Supper, following approval by the Church Council. 4. That churches would also identify, within their “Members”, those who are 18 or older, who profess faith in Christ, as “Voting Members”. 5. That churches be encouraged to meet with young people before they turn 18 (or as part of their ongoing discipleship program) to help them understand the responsibilities of voting and serving within the church. 6. That the CRCA, for Synodical quota and record keeping, require from churches both “Members” (total) and “Voting Members.” Synod decided: 7. That churches recognise and celebrate the faith development of covenant children at multiple stages in their journey. 8. That churches make themselves aware of the alternate form for Public Profession of Faith (Appendix 1) The following recommendation lapsed: 9. That Synod adopt the changes to the church order outlined in section 5 of this report. [Minutes Article 48: Children at the Lord’s Supper (Membership) [Report 1, Convenor Rev Ben Murphy] The following motion was defeated: 10. That given the changes made at Synod 2022 and reaffirmed at Synod 2024 the Church Order be amended as follows: Article 62 – Admission to Communicant Membership a. The session shall examine baptised members who wish to become communicant members concerning their motives, doctrine and life. Subject to satisfactory assessment of their professed faith, baptised members shall become communicant members. This may be celebrated on professing their faith in a public worship service in accordance with the form for the public profession of faith prescribed by the Synod. Synod adopted the following motion by the required 2/3rd majority for Church Order changes: 11. That given the changes made at Synod 2022 and reaffirmed at Synod 2024 the Church Order be amended as follows: Article 62 – Admission to Communicant Membership a. The session shall examine baptised members who wish to become communicant members concerning their motives, doctrine and life. Subject to satisfactory assessment, baptised members shall become communicant members on professing their faith. Sessions will do this in accordance with their local church regulations as prescribed by the synod. Article 16: Local Church Outreach [Report 12, Convenor – Rev Joshua Hartog] (Minutes Article 16) Synod decided: 1. To receive this report. 2. To approve the work done by the Local Church Outreach Coordinator. The following motion was lost: 3. To continue the position of the Local Church Outreach Coordinator. As a result, the following recommendation lapsed: 4. To appoint a new Local Church Outreach Coordinator. Article 17: Church Planting Taskforce [Report 13, Convenor – Rev KJ Tromp] (Minutes Article 17) Synod decided: 1. To receive this report. 2. To give approval for the CPT to encourage church planting amongst our churches via the strategy presented in our report. 3. To set up a Church Planting Fund, administered by the denominational treasurer, for the purpose of storing unspent funding beyond budgetary periods. 4. To set aside a time of prayer at Synod to ask God to pour out his Spirit on our churches so that more people may be reached, more churches planted as a result, that the hard labour of our churches may be fruitful, and that we continue to honour him with our sincere effort to reach the lost. 5. To allow a total budget allocation of $100,000 for the next triennium. 6. To approve a CPT administration budget of $7,000 to cover committee meetings & travel for the triennium 2024-2027. 7. To re-appoint the Church Planting Taskforce under the supervision of GROW. Article 18: Evaluate the Cost of SIC Committee [Report 6, Convenor – Rev. Jack Kapinga] (Minutes Article 18) Synod decided: 1. To receive the report. 2. To budget for and offer to compensate the Church in which the Chairman of SIC serves by an amount of up to 15% of Minimum Stipend for the duration of his term of service. 3. To request the SIC to produce a handbook for Ministers and Elders outlining the role and responsibilities of Moderamen/SIC and the definite and possible costs for those who serve in this capacity and for their Churches. 4. To include in the job description of the Chairman of Synod/SIC, the expectation that they will serve as a Mentor to the next Chairman of Synod/SIC. 5. That: - a) Any office-bearer who serves on SIC will not be expected to serve on any other Synodical Committee during their term. - b) Classes will be informed by the Synodical Administrator when an office-bearer in their Classis is serving on SIC and offer to relieve them of other Classis responsibilities during their term. - c) Churches will be informed by the Synodical Administrator when their Minister or Elder is serving on SIC and urged to relieve them of certain responsibilities during their term. 6. To instruct the Synodical Administrator to survey the Churches after each Synod to determine if there are willing people within the denomination who can be called upon to assist the SIC when needed, such as those who can provide professional advice such as lawyers or those who have time and ability to complete more time-consuming tasks such as retired ministers. 7. That the rules for electing the Moderamen of Synod be amended to say that once a delegate is elected, any other office-bearers from that delegate’s Church are withdrawn from the election process. Article 19: Human Resources Study Committee [Report 8, Convenor – Chris Bongers] (Minutes Article 19) Synod decided: 1. To receive this report. 2. To direct the Business and Finance Committee (BFC), while establishing how best to financially and legally structure the overseas missions of the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia (CRCA), to also seek legal advice on: - a. The best company structure for employment purposes - b. the best model of membership for such a company or companies involving members of the BFC and Synodical Interim Committee (SIC) - c. any changes needed to the Church Order to reflect the legal structure of the company. 3. That once the company structure has been resolved, employment of staff be moved to the new company (Company). 4. That once the company structure has been resolved, all employees be placed on new contracts consistent with current employment standards, without change to existing additional benefits. 5. That each delegated subcommittee continue in their role as manager of the employee, following policies and procedures as set out by the Company. 6. That initially the BFC, and eventually the Company, in consultation with the Human Resources Study Committee (HRSC) make arrangements to either outsource the human resource function (excluding payroll and leave management), or seek a consultancy arrangement with, a likeminded organization with more human resource experience. This arrangement would be on the basis of a fee for service and would be available to the BFC, HRSC or Company and other committees or work groups to manage denominational employees and to the HRSC to develop systems, documentation and guidelines. 7. To make a budget allocation of $20,000 for the first year of engagement and $5,000 for subsequent years be made available to the BFC, HRSC or the Company for procuring these services. The additional funds in the first year is to establish consistency in current employment documents and working with committees and workgroups on implementation. 8. That a secure employment cloud environment be set up for long term storage of employee information and records, with access granted to the service provider, BFC or Company, relevant committees and CRCA employees. 9. To ask the HRSC to work with the Synod approved employer, workgroups and committees to establish: - a. a suitable job/position description format to be used for all denominational employees. - b. suitable guidelines for management of the human resources functions. - c. a suitable employee review system and templates. 10. To charge workgroups and committees to: - a. establish standardized job/position descriptions with current denominational employees, that accurately represent the tasks being undertaken by the employee. - b. ensure job/position descriptions clearly articulate and identify the employer and the reporting lines for employment purposes. - c. implement the guidelines into their practices of managing denominational employees and employment. - d. establish standardized review templates and procedures with committees and workgroups that employ denominational workers. 11. That current practices of Classis led employee reviews be changed to performance reviews by committees with denominational employees or by the HRSC. 12. That once the proper legal structure has been established, to charge the HRSC to work with the BFC or Company, committees and working groups to meet employer obligations. 13. To approve the establishment of human resource documents, policies and procedures to meet these obligations during the next inter-synodical period. 14. That the Human Resources Committee report on the progress of development and implementation of human resources functions at the 2027 Synod. Article 20: Candidacy Committee [Report 14, Convenor – Rev Josh Hartog] (Minutes Article 22, 25 & 41) Synod decided: 1. To receive this report. Regarding Interstate Students: 2. To actively invest in the development of relationships between Candidates, the Candidacy Committee (CC) and existing ordained ministers and ministry workers, by encouraging Candidates each year to attend Recharge and Synod, plus the RTC Preaching Conference. 3. To set aside $5000 per year to cover the cost of Candidates attending these conferences. Regarding Vicariates: 4. To approve funding for up to six (6) vicars for the next triennium up to $80,000 per vicariate. 5. To authorize the Committee to approach the Business and Finance Committee if more vicariates are needed for further funding. 6. To continue to allow a further $20,000 be made available for the use of a smaller church training a vicar, for the cost of suitable housing. Regarding the RTC: 7. To thank the RTC Board for their faithful oversight of the RTC and its Reformed emphasis. 8. To thank the current Faculty, including guest lecturers, for their faithful work and diligence in training ministry workers. 9. To thank the current ancillary staff for their supportive work at the RTC. 10. To continue our previous levels of financial contribution to the RTC of $140,000 per year from quota, as well as the current level of prescribed offerings (approximately $95,000 per year). 11. To match the RCNZ’s generous support of the new Systematic Theology lecturer to the amount of $50,000 per year. Regarding Ministers in Training Overture 12. To adopt the “minister in training” program as outlined in Appendix 1 of this report. Regarding the Committee’s ongoing work 13. To set aside the amount of $15,000 for the next triennium for the costs of personality assessment and/or training in the use of Personality Profiles and profile resources as well as providing assistance in counselling for ministry Candidates. 14. To set aside $5000 for meeting costs for the Committee for the next triennium. 15. To re-appoint the Committee. [Minutes Article 41 - Candidacy Committee Ad Hoc Committee] Synod Decided: 16. To contribute to the RTC $140,000 per year from ministry share, as well as the current level of prescribed offerings. Article 21: IndiWay [Report 9, Convenor – Rev Bert Kuipers] (Minutes Article 23 & 37) Synod decided: 1. To receive this report and its appendices. 2. To ratify the change in name from GOSPEL to IndiWay. 3. To thank the Lord that he has blessed the work of IndiWay with numerical and spiritual growth and that he has abundantly provided the material resources these last three years. 4. To acknowledge with gratitude and humility the significant role of the World Transform committee in the work that’s done in India amongst poor and marginalized tribal people. The following motion was withdrawn: 5. To re-affirm the plans for IndiWay to proceed to do a feasibility study for a mission training facility for its ministry workers. Synod agreed: 6. To thank the RTC for their support and encouragement for the tribal mission work in India 7. To approve of the work of the committee. 8. To invite the four Classes not yet represented on the IndiWay to appoint a mission minded person. 9. To re-appoint all the IndiWay subcommittee members. Note – Please also refer to Article 22. - Minutes Article 37: World Transform Ad Hoc Committee] Article 22: World Transform [Report 10, Convenor – Rev Bert Kuipers] (Minutes Article 24, 37 & 43) Synod decided: 1. To receive this report and its appendices. 2. To approve the work in general of World Transform. 3. To approve the auditor’s report and all the financial undertakings of the World Transform. 4. To thank and commend the members for their efforts over the last inter-synodical period. 5. To thank the churches for their Kingdom giving over these last three years. [Minutes Article 37: World Transform and IndiWay Ad Hoc Committee – Reporter: Craig van Echten] Synod decided that: 6. Synod recognises and appreciates the substantial and enthusiastic support for and management of the Denomination’s overseas diaconal and gospel works conducted through IndiWay and World Transform. Synod also recognises the disquiet in successive Synod meetings concerning late and incomplete financial reporting on those works. It is the desire of Synod to see procedures implemented which will enable IndiWay and World Transform to demonstrate effective governance of the finances committed to them, and that such procedures be as un-burdensome as possible. Synod therefore requests that the following process be implemented: 7. World Transform closes any bank accounts that it operates independently from the CRCA by 30 September 2024. This would include any bank accounts that are operated under the ABN 29 436 637 858 (the Unincorporated Association called World Transform). 8. World Transform cancels the ABN 29 436 637 858 by 30 September 2024. 9. [Minutes Article 42. SCAC Ad Hoc Committee – Reporter Frank van den Bos] Synod decided: 1. To establish a Safe Church Review Committee, consisting of one member from each Classis, with the following mandate: - a. To thoroughly review and edit the proposed 15 new Safe Church policies to ensure that they conform to a Confessional Reformed Worldview. - i. Specifically, the committee must seek to ensure that these policies: 1. Are fully consistent with the confessions of our Reformed Churches. 2. Avoid over-commitment to measures inconsistent with a reformed worldview. 3. Recognise and promote the central authority and God-given role of parents in protecting their children, as well as recognising the responsibility of the elders to oversee the church, and the responsibility of the whole church to provide a safeplace for all who attend. 4. Submit to the mandates of civil authorities at all points except where those mandates contradict scripture. 5. Consistently honour and respect civil authorities at all points. 6. As much as possible, can be easily read, understood, and applied in a local church setting by a large or small church. - ii. As the committee reviews and edits each of the 15 policies, they will be circulated to our Classes on a rolling basis for majority approval and adoption. - b. To include a member of SCAC as a committee member, and to ensure that edits are in line with the SCAC mandate - c. To conduct a thorough investigation of how other reformed denominations in Australia and the world are responding to these challenges, and provide a report at the next Synod - d. That the committee conducts a general theological review of all aspects of the SCAC mandate. - e. That the committee conducts all of these tasks with full and thankful recognition and appreciation for the great service rendered to our churches by all members of SCAC and its predecessors. 2. That churches provisionally adopt the CRCA National Safeguarding Policy, as amended by this ad hoc committee, being also subject to the overarching review by the Safe Church Review committee. 3. That churches provisionally adopt the CRCA Code of Conduct, as amended by this ad hoc committee, being also subject to the overarching review by the Safe Church Review committee. 4. To provide the draft policies referred to in Recommendations 21-33 in the report to our churches as a provisional help for our churches to ensure that they are meeting their legal responsibilities. 5. That, after the 15 policies have been properly approved, churches adopt these policies and discontinue the use of the current Denominational Safeguarding Children and Vulnerable People policy. 6. To urge churches to minimise the risk of claims involving vicarious liability by ensuring that all staff and volunteers appointed by church leadership are well known to the church and hold current working with children cards (or similar). 7. To urge churches to make sure that all guest speakers are properly vetted and adhere to all relevant legal requirements as designated by state law. 8. Colin Pretorius 15. Youth Teaching Resources Committee (RCYC Subcommittee) Rev. Nathanael Remminga (CPC) Mr. Kasha Schubert (Vic Gippsland) Mr. Micah Vanderkolk (NSW) Miss. Zoe de Witte (Qld) Rev. Ben Murphy (Convenor, WA) 16. Financial Barriers to Ministry Training Committee Rev. Nathanael Remminga (Convenor) Rev. Clinton Berends (Ex Officio) Rev. Jack Kapinga 17. Safe Church Review Committee Rev. Isaac Overton Rev. Craig van Echten Rev. Isaac Lee Rev. Richard Schoenmaker Mr. Frank van den Bos Mr. John van Dijk Classis NSW – TBA Article 41: Next Synod (Minutes Article 51) Synod decided that Classis NSW be charged to convene the 2027 Synod. It was noted that the Wollongong CRC had offered to be the convening church subject to session approval. Synod agreed that an option would be to hold the Synod in a conference centre and noted that this had been budgeted for. Article 42: Vote of thanks (Minutes Article 52) At various stages during the last day of Synod 2024 the Chairman asked Synod to express thanks to those involved in the organising and running of Synod. This included the organising committee, those who worked so tirelessly in providing for our physical needs, our transport and especially from the kitchen and also those who provided billets for the many delegates, musicians and those helping out with sound and IT. He also gave a vote of thanks for support provided by the Moderamen, Synodical Treasurer, Synodical Administrator, the delegates, advisers and fraternal delegates. In response, on behalf of the delegates, the Vice-Chairman, Rev. Andrew Nugteren, thanked the Chairman for the efficient and competent way in which he had led this Synod. Article 43: Close of Synod (Minutes Article 53) The Chairman of Synod, Rev. John Zuidema gave the closing address and after prayer, declared the 2024 Synod closed at 5:30pm.
